property.value: Micrometer is an open-source dimensional metrics instrumentation library for microservices and other applications. It provides a simple and consistent API for collecting application metrics, such as response times, error rates, and throughput, from various monitoring systems. Micrometer supports a wide range of monitoring systems, including Prometheus, Graphite, InfluxDB, and more, allowing developers to choose the system that best fits their needs.

An example of using Micrometer is to instrument a microservice to collect response time metrics. By adding a few lines of code, developers can measure the time taken by different parts of the service, such as database queries, external API calls, or specific methods. These metrics can then be visualized and analyzed using a monitoring system like Prometheus or Graphite. This helps in identifying slow-performing components, detecting anomalies, and optimizing the overall system performance.

Micrometer simplifies the process of instrumenting code to collect metrics, making it easier to monitor and analyze the performance and behavior of applications. It offers a vendor-neutral abstraction layer that decouples the application code from the underlying monitoring system. This allows developers to switch between monitoring systems without modifying their code. Micrometer provides a rich set of features, including support for timers, counters, gauges, histograms, and distribution summaries. It also offers advanced capabilities like dimensional metrics, which enable tagging and filtering of metrics based on custom dimensions. By using Micrometer, developers can gain valuable insights into their applications' performance, identify bottlenecks, and make data-driven decisions to optimize their systems.

element.name: e-Timestamp Creation
element.documentation:
Definition: e-Timestamp Creation ABB is an Application Service that enables the recording of the date and time when a specific electronic document, data or transaction is created or modified. This ABB verifies the existence, integrity, and authenticity of an electronic document, data or transaction.
Source: eIDAS - REGULATION (EU) No 910/2014 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 23 July 2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market and repealing Directive 1999/93/EC.
Source reference: http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=uriserv%3AOJ.L_.2014.257.01.0073.01.ENG
Additional information: An ‘electronic time stamp’ means data in electronic form which binds other data in electronic form to a particular time establishing evidence that the latter data existed at that time.
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): DigiStamp eTimeStamp® - DigiStamp eTimeStamp® protects the intellectual property in any computer file: • Use Desktop and Web applications for on-demand protection; • Plug the Timestamp Authority into the automated systems. Plug-in rigorous implementation of US & EU standards: • Secure, reliable, RFC 3161 timestamp cloud service; • Archiving and Hash Chaining keyless security; • Elliptic Curve Upgrade; Implementation of the Internet Engineering Task Force's RFC 3161 means DigiStamp timestamps are understood by data validation systems the world over: • Implementation of ANSI X9.95 further increases the compatibility of our timestamps; • Compliance with IETF RFC 3628 gives credence to the trustworthiness of our Time Stamp Authorities.; • Conformance to IETF RFC 3126 makes our timestamps usable for long-term, legally binding agreements. https://www.digistamp.com/
IoP Dimension: Behavioral IoP
LOST view: Technical view - application
Interoperability saliency: The e-Timestamp Creation Service ABB is salient for technical interoperability because it provides the functionalities required for e-Timestamp creation service.

element.name: e-Archiving
element.documentation:
Definition: e-Archiving ABB is an Application Service enabling the permanent or long-term storage of selected (by an authority) electronic documents or information for preservation purposes like their enduring research value and memory aid.
Source: ISA2 - EIA Action
Source reference: https://ec.europa.eu/isa2/actions/towards-european-interoperability-architecture_en/
Synonym: Preservation Service
Additional information: The EIRA(c) differentiates between document management, record management and e-archiving as follows: - Document management is primarily about day-to-day use of electronic documents (create/update/delete/versioning) within the operational environment; - Record management is primarily about ensuring that information (e.g. in form of an electronic document or database record) is available for business and legal purposes (e.g. to proof and track the handling of contracts). If an electronic document or information is becoming a record (an authority declares it as a record) that electronic document or information needs to be handled by the record management service (based on specific business or legal reasons (e.g. contract negotiation)); - e-Archiving is primarily about storing records which have been selected (by an authority) for permanent or long-term preservation due to their enduring research value and as a memory aid. An electronic document or information which a) is managed by the document management service or the record management service and b) is no longer needed for business or legal purposes or day-to-day activities, and c) still has value for research purposes or as a memory aid, the electronic document should be managed by the e-archiving service”.
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): CEF eArchiving: eArchiving provides the core specifications, software, training and knowledge to tackle the challenge of short, medium and long-term data management and reuse in a sustainable, authentic, cost-efficient, manageable and interoperable way. https://ec.europa.eu/cefdigital/wiki/display/CEFDIGITAL/eArchiving
IoP Dimension: Behavioral IoP
LOST view: Technical view - application
Interoperability saliency: The e-Archiving Service ABB is salient for technical interoperability because it provides and shares the functionality for the long-term or permanent preservation of records and information in electronic form in order to ensure their temporal egibility, reliability and integrity as stated in the EIF: "Legislation requires that decisions and data are stored and can be accessed for a specified time. This means that records and information in electronic form held by public administrations for the purpose of documenting procedures and decisions must be preserved and be converted, where necessary, to new media when old media become obsolete. The goal is to ensure that records and other forms of information keep their legibility, reliability and integrity and can be accessed as long as needed subject to security and privacy provisions."

element.name: Distributed Ledger
element.documentation:
Definition: A distributed ledger is a decentralized database that maintains a continuously growing list of records, called blocks, which are linked and secured using cryptography. Unlike traditional centralized databases, a distributed ledger is replicated and synchronized across multiple nodes or computers in a network, ensuring transparency, immutability, and consensus among participants.
Source: Investopedia
Source reference: https://www.investopedia.com/terms/d/distributed-ledger.asp
Additional information: Distributed ledgers, often based on blockchain technology, enable participants to have a shared view of the database without relying on a central authority. Each participant in the network has a copy of the entire ledger, and any changes or additions to the ledger require consensus among the participants. This distributed and consensus-driven approach enhances security, as altering a single record would require tampering with all copies of the ledger across the network. Distributed ledgers find applications in various industries, including finance, supply chain management, healthcare, and voting systems, where transparency, traceability, and trust are crucial.
Example: One example of a distributed ledger application is cryptocurrency, such as Bitcoin. In the Bitcoin network, transactions are recorded in blocks, which are added to the blockchain by miners. Each participant in the network has a copy of the entire blockchain, ensuring transparency and preventing double-spending. Another example is supply chain management, where distributed ledgers can track the movement of goods from the point of origin to the end consumer, providing transparency and reducing fraud.
LOST view: TVA-Trust Enablers [Motivation]

element.name: Vocabulary Hub
element.documentation:
Definition: The Vocabulary Hub is an IT concept that refers to a centralized repository or platform designed to store, manage, and provide access to a wide range of vocabularies or terminologies used in various domains. It serves as a comprehensive and standardized source of terms, definitions, and relationships between concepts, enabling efficient data integration, interoperability, and semantic understanding across different systems and applications.
Source: W3C
Source reference: https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-hub/
Additional information: The Vocabulary Hub acts as a central hub for vocabularies, offering a unified and consistent way to define and organize terms. It provides a common framework for describing concepts, their properties, and relationships, facilitating data sharing and integration between different systems and applications. The hub typically supports various standard formats and protocols for vocabulary representation and exchange, such as RDF, SKOS, and SPARQL, ensuring compatibility and interoperability. It also offers functionalities like versioning, access control, and search capabilities, making it easier for users to discover, reuse, and maintain vocabularies.
Example: An example of the Vocabulary Hub in action is a healthcare system that integrates data from multiple sources, such as electronic health records, medical devices, and research databases. By utilizing the Vocabulary Hub, the system can harmonize and align the terminologies used in these disparate sources, enabling accurate and meaningful data exchange. This allows healthcare professionals to access comprehensive patient information, perform advanced analytics, and improve decision-making processes. Additionally, the Vocabulary Hub facilitates the development of innovative applications and services that leverage the shared vocabulary knowledge, promoting collaboration and interoperability within the healthcare ecosystem.
LOST view: TVA-Knowledge Discovery Enablers [Motivation]

It is cross-sectorial and can be expanded beyond the current scope of life events set out in the Single Digital Gateway Regulation. It puts into practice the Once-Only Principle, which states that citizens should not be forced to provide information to authorities if another authority already holds that information in electronic format.

element.name: e-Signature Verification and Validation
element.documentation:
Definition: e-Signature Verification and Validation Service ABB is an Application Service that enables the process of verifying and confirming that an electronic signature or a seal is valid.
Source: eIDAS - REGULATION (EU) No 910/2014 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 23 July 2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market and repealing Directive 1999/93/EC.
Source reference: http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=uriserv%3AOJ.L_.2014.257.01.0073.01.ENG
Additional information: An ‘electronic signature’ means data in electronic form which is attached to or logically associated with other data in electronic form and which is used by the signatory to sign. ‘Validation’ means the process of verifying and confirming that an electronic signature or a seal is valid.
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): CEF eSignature DSS - DSS (Digital Signature Services) is an open-source software library for electronic signature creation and validation. DSS supports the creation and verification of interoperable and secure electronic signatures in line with European legislation. In particular, DSS aims to follow the eIDAS Regulation and related standards closely. DSS can be re-used in an IT solution for electronic signatures to ensure that signatures are created and verified in line with European legislation and standards. DSS allows re-use in a variety of different ways: in an applet, in a stand-alone application or in a server application. DSS can also be used as a reference implementation for IT solutions which do not directly re-use it. CEF eSignature's DSS open-source library delivers the following benefits to its users: • Open-source software under LGPL 2.1, a non-viral open source license; • Interoperability of the e-signatures; • Supports both e-signatures and e-seals; • Validation of countersignatures and multiple signatures; • Alignment with the eIDAS Regulation and related standards; • Supports EU standards on: o Signature formats and packaging methods; o Signature validation procedures; • Validation relying on Member States' trusted lists: o Status of trust service providers/trust service, compensation of information, path validation. https://ec.europa.eu/cefdigital/wiki/display/CEFDIGITAL/eSignaturefile:///C:/Users/bocquilp/Downloads/DSS(ServiceOfferingDescription)%20(v0.03)%20(5).pdf

element.name: European Interoperability TestBed
element.documentation:
Description: The Interoperability Test Bed is a service offered by the European Commission’s DIGIT to facilitate the conformance testing of IT systems. The Test Bed is itself a software system that can be both downloaded and installed locally, but also reused through a shared online installation operated by DIGIT. property.value: The Interoperability Test Bed is a service offered by the European Commission’s DIGIT to facilitate the conformance testing of IT systems. The Test Bed is itself a software system that can be both downloaded and installed locally, but also reused through a shared online installation operated by DIGIT. It offers an intuitive web user interface that allows administrators to define their project’s overall testing setup as well as users to connect and run tests.

In terms of the testing approach it follows, the Test Bed is typically used to exchange messages with the software systems being tested, supporting both the sending and receiving of messages, validating all steps against the target specification and according to the specific scenario’s expectations. Such scenarios can focus on technical details but can also be defined at business-level, exposing details only when needed to troubleshoot failures. Furthermore, tests can be designed to cover both normal flows but also edge cases and error scenarios that would be otherwise difficult to replicate.

element.name: Apache NiFi
element.documentation:
Description: Apache NiFi is an open-source data integration and data flow automation tool that provides a visual interface to easily manage and control the movement of data between different systems. It allows users to design, build, and execute data flows, known as data pipelines, using a web-based graphical user interface (GUI). NiFi supports a wide range of data sources, destinations, and processors, enabling efficient data ingestion, transformation, routing, and monitoring.
Additional information: Apache NiFi is designed to handle real-time data streaming and batch processing, making it suitable for use cases such as IoT data collection, log aggregation, data migration, and data transformation. It provides a scalable and reliable platform for managing data flows across various systems, including databases, cloud storage, messaging systems, and more. NiFi's GUI allows users to visually create and modify data pipelines, making it accessible to both technical and non-technical users. It offers features like data provenance, security, data lineage, and extensive monitoring capabilities. NiFi also supports data governance and compliance requirements through features like data encryption, access control, and auditing.
Example: An example application of Apache NiFi is in a data lake architecture. NiFi can be used to ingest data from various sources like sensors, social media feeds, and databases into a centralized data lake. It can then perform data transformations, filtering, and enrichment before storing the processed data in a suitable format for downstream analytics. NiFi's visual interface makes it easy to design and manage complex data flows, ensuring efficient and reliable data movement within the data lake ecosystem.

element.name: Message Broker
element.documentation:
Definition: A message broker is an intermediary software component that facilitates communication between different applications by enabling asynchronous message-based communication. It acts as a central hub where applications can publish messages and subscribe to receive messages based on specific criteria. The message broker ensures reliable delivery of messages, decouples applications from each other, and provides features like message routing, transformation, and filtering.
Source: Techopedia
Source reference: https://www.techopedia.com/definition/28536/message-broker
Additional information: Message brokers play a crucial role in distributed systems and service-oriented architectures, where multiple applications need to exchange information in a scalable and decoupled manner. They provide a reliable and efficient way to handle the communication between applications, allowing them to operate independently and asynchronously. Message brokers can handle various messaging patterns like publish/subscribe, request/reply, and point-to-point, and often support different messaging protocols such as AMQP, MQTT, or JMS.
Example: An example of a message broker is Apache Kafka, a popular distributed streaming platform. In this scenario, multiple producers can publish messages to Kafka topics, and multiple consumers can subscribe to these topics to receive the messages. The message broker ensures that messages are reliably stored and delivered to the appropriate consumers, even if they are offline or experiencing temporary failures. This enables real-time data processing, event-driven architectures, and scalable data streaming applications.

element.name: Federated Data Catalogue Management
element.documentation:
Definition: Federated Data Catalogue Management refers to the practice of centrally managing and organizing metadata about data assets across multiple data catalogues within an organization. It involves creating a unified view of data assets, their attributes, and relationships, while allowing decentralized control and ownership of individual catalogues.
Source: Techopedia
Source reference: https://www.techopedia.com/definition/33133/federated-data-catalog-management
Additional information: In a federated data catalogue management approach, each data catalogue retains its autonomy and maintains its own metadata, but a central management system is responsible for aggregating and harmonizing the metadata from all catalogues. This allows users to search, discover, and understand data assets across different catalogues, promoting data sharing, collaboration, and governance. The federated approach enables organizations to leverage existing catalogues, avoid data duplication, and maintain data lineage and provenance. It also facilitates compliance with data regulations and standards by providing a comprehensive view of data assets.
Example: An organization with multiple business units may have separate data catalogues for each unit. With federated data catalogue management, a central system can integrate metadata from all catalogues, enabling users to search and discover data assets across units. For example, a data analyst in one business unit can easily find and access relevant datasets from another unit's catalogue without needing direct access to that catalogue. This promotes cross-functional collaboration, reduces data silos, and improves overall data governance and utilization.

element.name: Workflow Management
element.documentation:
Definition: A Workflow Management Application Service, also known as Orchestration Application Service, refers to a software solution or service that enables the design, execution, and coordination of workflows within an organization. element.name: Containers Orchestrator
element.documentation:
Definition: Containers Orchestrator is a software tool or platform that automates the deployment, management, and scaling of containerized applications. It provides a centralized control plane to efficiently manage and coordinate the deployment and operation of containers across a cluster of machines or nodes.
Source: Wikipedia
Source reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Container_orchestration
Additional information: Containers Orchestrator simplifies the management of containerized applications by abstracting away the underlying infrastructure complexities. It enables efficient resource utilization, load balancing, high availability, and fault tolerance. The orchestrator handles tasks such as container scheduling, service discovery, networking, storage management, and health monitoring. It allows developers to focus on application development and deployment, while ensuring scalability, resilience, and ease of management.
Example: One popular example of a Containers Orchestrator is Kubernetes. It provides a robust and scalable platform for managing containerized applications. With Kubernetes, developers can define the desired state of their application using declarative configuration files, and the orchestrator takes care of deploying and managing the containers accordingly. It offers features like automatic scaling, rolling updates, service discovery, and load balancing, making it easier to deploy and manage applications in a distributed environment.

element.name: Trusted Digital Repositories
element.documentation:
Definition: Trusted Digital Repositories refer to specialized eArchiving application services that are designed to preserve and provide long-term access to digital objects, such as documents, datasets, multimedia files, and other forms of digital content. These repositories follow established standards, best practices, and guidelines to ensure the integrity, authenticity, and usability of the archived materials over time. They employ robust storage, metadata management, and preservation strategies to safeguard the long-term viability and accessibility of digital assets. Trusted Digital Repositories play a crucial role in the preservation and curation of digital heritage, research data, and other valuable digital resources.

element.name: Operational tax application
element.documentation:
Definition: An Operational Tax Application refers to the utilization or consumption of features provided by an operational tax application system. This system facilitates the management of all taxpayers' applications submitted to the Tax Authorities.
Source: Custom Definition
Source reference: N/A
Additional information: Operational tax applications are designed to streamline and automate the process of tax management. They provide a platform where taxpayers can submit their tax applications, track their status, and manage their tax-related information. These applications are equipped with features that allow for efficient data management, accurate tax calculations, and timely submissions. They are typically used by tax authorities and organizations to manage their tax operations effectively and ensure compliance with tax regulations.
Example: A multinational corporation uses an operational tax application to manage its tax obligations across different countries. The application allows the corporation to submit tax applications, track their status, and manage tax-related information in a centralized manner.
A tax authority uses an operational tax application to process tax applications submitted by taxpayers. The application automates the process of checking the accuracy of the tax calculations, ensuring timely submissions, and managing the data of the taxpayers.

element.name: Apache Atlas
element.documentation:
Description: Apache Atlas is an open-source metadata management and governance framework for enterprises. It provides a scalable platform to capture, manage, and govern metadata about data assets across various systems in an organization. By enabling metadata management, Apache Atlas helps organizations gain insights into their data assets, ensure data quality, and enforce data governance policies.
Additional information: Apache Atlas allows organizations to create a centralized repository of metadata that describes their data assets, such as databases, tables, columns, and relationships between them. It supports a wide range of data platforms and technologies, including Hadoop, relational databases, cloud storage, and more. With Apache Atlas, organizations can define and enforce data governance policies, such as data classification, access controls, and data lineage. It provides a comprehensive set of features for data discovery, data lineage tracking, data quality monitoring, and metadata search. Apache Atlas also integrates with other data management and governance tools, enabling seamless interoperability in the data ecosystem.
Example: An organization can use Apache Atlas to track the lineage of a specific data asset, such as a customer's personal information stored in a database. It can capture metadata about the source of the data, the transformations applied to it, and the systems that consume this data. This allows organizations to understand the origin and usage of data, ensuring compliance with regulations like GDPR. Additionally, Apache Atlas can be used to classify sensitive data, apply access controls, and monitor data quality, providing a holistic view of data assets and enabling effective data governance.

Source: https://atlas.apache.org/

element.name: SEED
element.documentation:
Description: SEED (System for Exchange of Excise Data) is a tool that represents the use or consumption of features provided by the SEED enabling the classification of excise duty in compliance with the defined European standards and legislation.
Additional information: SEED is an integral part of the Excise Movement and Control System (EMCS), which is a computerized system for monitoring the movement of excise goods within the EU. It is used by economic operators and national administrations to ensure that excise duties are correctly applied and collected. SEED is used to validate the excise numbers of the consignor, consignee, and transporter, and to provide a risk analysis for the consignment. It is a crucial tool for ensuring the correct application of excise duties and for preventing fraud.
Example: For instance, a company that produces alcoholic beverages in France and wants to transport them to a warehouse in Germany would use the SEED system. The French company would enter the details of the consignment into the EMCS, which would then use SEED to validate the excise numbers of the French company, the German warehouse, and the transporter. SEED would also provide a risk analysis for the consignment. Once the consignment has been delivered, the German warehouse would confirm receipt via the EMCS, and the excise duty would be paid in Germany.
Publisher: European Commission
Source: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/business/excise-duties-alcohol-tobacco-energy/excise-movement-control-system_en

element.name: European Blockchain Services Infrastructure
element.documentation:
Description: The European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI) is an IT concept that aims to provide a secure and scalable infrastructure for blockchain-based services across Europe. It is a network of distributed nodes that enables the interoperability of different blockchain platforms and facilitates the development and deployment of blockchain applications in various domains.
Additional information: The EBSI is being developed by the European Commission in collaboration with member states and industry partners. It aims to promote the adoption of blockchain technology in the public sector by providing a trusted and efficient infrastructure. The EBSI leverages blockchain's decentralized and immutable nature to enhance transparency, security, and trust in digital transactions. It enables the creation of smart contracts, digital identity management, supply chain traceability, and other applications that require secure and tamper-proof data exchange. The EBSI also supports the integration of existing systems and services, ensuring seamless interoperability between different blockchain networks.
Example: One example of the application of the EBSI is in the field of public procurement. By utilizing blockchain technology, the EBSI can enable transparent and auditable procurement processes, reducing fraud and increasing efficiency. It can provide a secure and tamper-proof record of all transactions, ensuring the integrity of the procurement process. Additionally, the EBSI can facilitate cross-border transactions, allowing suppliers from different countries to participate in procurement procedures without the need for complex paperwork and intermediaries.
Publisher: European Commission
Source: https://ec.europa.eu/cefdigital/wiki/display/CEFDIGITAL/European+Blockchain+Services+Infrastructure

element.name: Kubernetes
element.documentation:
Description: Kubernetes is an open-source container orchestration platform that automates the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications. It provides a highly scalable and flexible environment for running, managing, and scaling applications across a cluster of machines.
Additional information: Kubernetes simplifies the management of containerized applications by abstracting away the underlying infrastructure complexities. It allows developers to define their application's desired state and Kubernetes takes care of deploying and maintaining that state. It provides features like automatic scaling, load balancing, self-healing, and rolling updates, ensuring high availability and fault tolerance. Kubernetes also enables efficient resource utilization by intelligently scheduling containers across the cluster based on resource requirements. It supports various container runtimes and can be deployed on-premises, in the cloud, or in hybrid environments.
Example: For example, a company running a microservices-based architecture can use Kubernetes to deploy and manage their containerized services. They can define the desired number of replicas for each service, specify resource requirements, and set up health checks. Kubernetes will then ensure that the desired state is maintained, automatically scaling the services based on demand, distributing traffic across replicas, and restarting failed containers. It provides a centralized control plane to monitor and manage the entire application infrastructure, making it easier to scale and update the system without downtime.
Publisher: Kubernetes.io
Source: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/what-is-kubernetes/

element.name: Digital Certification Timestamp
element.documentation:
Definition: e-Timestamp Verification and Validation Service ABB is an Application Service verifing timestamps used for establishing evidence that a give piece of data existed at a given point in time. An ‘electronic time stamp’ means data in electronic form which binds other data in electronic form to a particular time establishing evidence that the latter data existed at that time.
Source: eIDAS - REGULATION (EU) No 910/2014 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 23 July 2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market and repealing Directive 1999/93/EC.
Source reference: (http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=uriserv%3AOJ.L_.2014.257.01.0073.01.ENG)
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): OpenSSL timestamp verification - OpenSSL is an open-source tool that can be used to retrieve and verify digital timestamps.(https://wiki.openssl.org/index.php/Manual:Ts(1)) (https://www.digistamp.com/technical/software-alternatives/using-openssl-to-request-timestamps/)
eira:iopDimension: Behavioral IoP
LOST view: TVA-Trust Enablers [Motivation]

The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): OpenSSL timestamp verification - OpenSSL is an open-source tool that can be used to retrieve and verify digital timestamps.(https://wiki.openssl.org/index.php/Manual:Ts(1)) (https://www.digistamp.com/technical/software-alternatives/using-openssl-to-request-timestamps/)

This service is often used in the context of digital signatures and data integrity, where it is crucial to establish when a document was signed or when data was created or last modified. The timestamp is created by a trusted third party, known as a Timestamping Authority (TSA), which attests to the time and date the data was presented to it without any alterations. The TSA uses a cryptographic hash function to generate a unique hash of the submitted data, then signs this hash with its private key, creating a timestamp token that can be verified using the TSA's public key. This process ensures non-repudiation, meaning that the parties involved cannot deny the existence of the data at the time it was timestamped.

element.name: e-Seal Verification and Validation
element.documentation:
Definition: e-Seal Verification and Validation ABB is an Application Service that enables the functionality of the verification of documents that are signed electronically.
Source: eIDAS - REGULATION (EU) No 910/2014 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 23 July 2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market and repealing Directive 1999/93/EC.
Source reference: http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=uriserv%3AOJ.L_.2014.257.01.0073.01.ENG
Additional information: An ‘electronic seal' means data in electronic form, which is attached to or logically associated with other data in electronic form to ensure the latter’s origin and integrity. The ‘creator of a seal’ is a legal person who creates an electronic seal.
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): CEF eSignature DSS - DSS (Digital Signature Services) is an open-source software library for electronic signature creation and validation. DSS supports the creation and verification of interoperable and secure electronic signatures in line with European legislation. In particular, DSS aims to follow the eIDAS Regulation and related standards closely. DSS can be re-used in an IT solution for electronic signatures to ensure that signatures are created and verified in line with European legislation and standards. DSS allows re-use in a variety of different ways: in an applet, in a stand-alone application or in a server application. DSS can also be used as a reference implementation for IT solutions which do not directly re-use it. CEF eSignature's DSS open-source library delivers the following benefits to its users: • Open-source software under LGPL 2.1, a non-viral open source license; • Interoperability of the e-signatures; • Supports both e-signatures and e-seals; • Validation of countersignatures and multiple signatures; • Alignment with the eIDAS Regulation and related standards; • Supports EU standards on: o Signature formats and packaging methods; o Signature validation procedures; • Validation relying on Member States' trusted lists: o Status of trust service providers/trust service, compensation of information, path validation. https://ec.europa.eu/cefdigital/wiki/display/CEFDIGITAL/eSignaturefile:///C:/Users/bocquilp/Downloads/DSS(ServiceOfferingDescription)%20(v0.03)%20(5).pdf

element.name: FIWARE TRUE Connector
element.documentation:
Description: The FIWARE TRUE Connector is a software module that facilitates the exchange of data between FIWARE and the International Data Space (IDS) ecosystem. It provides a secure and reliable way to share data between different organizations, while ensuring that the data remains compliant with IDS standards.
Additional information: The FIWARE TRUE Connector is a key enabler for the IDS ecosystem, as it allows organizations to share data in a secure and compliant way. It is currently used by a number of organizations, including the European Commission and the City of Barcelona.
Example: The FIWARE TRUE Connector can be used to share data between different smart city applications. For example, it could be used to share data about traffic congestion between a traffic management system and a public transport app.

element.name: Tax Digital Information Gateway
element.documentation:
Description: The Tax Digital Information Gateway is a digital platform that facilitates tax administration by providing access to tax-related information owned by other Member States or different public administrations.
Additional information: The Tax Digital Information Gateway is a crucial tool in the modernization of tax administration. It enables seamless sharing and access to tax-related information across different jurisdictions, thereby enhancing transparency, efficiency, and cooperation among tax authorities. The gateway can provide information on a variety of tax-related matters, including income tax, corporate tax, value-added tax (VAT), and other forms of direct and indirect taxation. It is particularly useful in the context of cross-border transactions and operations, where tax-related information from different Member States may be required.
Example: For instance, if a business entity operates in multiple European Union Member States, the Tax Digital Information Gateway can provide the respective tax authorities with access to the necessary tax-related information from each jurisdiction. This can facilitate the process of tax assessment and collection, ensuring compliance with the tax laws of each Member State. Similarly, in the case of an individual taxpayer with income sources in different Member States, the gateway can provide the relevant tax authorities with access to the necessary income information, thereby facilitating the process of income tax assessment and collection.
Publisher: EU Taxation and Customs Union
Source: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/business/tax-cooperation-control/administrative-cooperation/enhanced-administrative-cooperation-field-direct-taxation_en

Description: An OAuth2/OpenID Connect server for IoT devices which use their private keys to request OAuth2 access tokens in order to access protected resources and websites or apps which retrieve user attributes.

element.name: Learning Platform System
element.documentation:
Definition: A Learning Platform System is a software application service that provides a comprehensive platform for managing and delivering learning content and experiences. It enables organizations to create, manage, and deliver various types of learning materials, such as courses, training modules, assessments, and educational resources. The Learning Platform System typically includes features such as content authoring, learner management, progress tracking, assessment tools, discussion forums, and collaboration capabilities. It supports both self-paced and instructor-led learning, fostering employee or user development, knowledge acquisition, and skill enhancement. The Learning Platform System application service facilitates efficient and effective learning experiences, enabling organizations to deliver training and educational programs in a centralized and scalable manner.

element.name: Docker Compose
element.documentation:
Description: Docker Compose is a tool that allows defining and running multi-container Docker applications. It uses a YAML file to configure the services, networks, and volumes required for the application, enabling easy deployment and management of complex containerized environments.
Additional information: Docker Compose simplifies the process of orchestrating multiple Docker containers by providing a declarative way to define the desired state of the application stack. The YAML file specifies the services, their dependencies, network connections, and storage volumes required for the application. Docker Compose then takes care of creating and managing the necessary containers, networks, and volumes, ensuring the defined services can communicate with each other. It allows developers to define the entire application stack as code, making it easy to reproduce and share the environment across different development stages or deployment environments. Docker Compose is particularly useful for development and testing scenarios where multiple services need to work together.
Example: An example of using Docker Compose is a web application that consists of a frontend service, a backend API service, and a database service. The Docker Compose file would define these services along with their configurations, dependencies, and network connections. By running a single command, Docker Compose would create and manage the necessary containers, networks, and volumes, setting up the complete application stack. This allows developers to easily spin up the entire environment on their local machines for development or testing purposes, ensuring all services are properly connected and functioning as expected.
Publisher: Docker Documentation
Source: https://docs.docker.com/compose/

element.name: Multimedia distribution
element.documentation:
Definition: Multimedia Distribution refers to a data management application service that facilitates the efficient and scalable distribution of multimedia content, such as audio, video, images, and other multimedia formats. It encompasses the storage, retrieval, and delivery of multimedia assets to end-users or target systems. This service typically involves the use of network infrastructure, content delivery networks (CDNs), and streaming technologies to ensure fast and reliable delivery of multimedia content across various devices and platforms. element.name: Fraunhofer AISEC Trusted Connector
element.documentation:
Description: The “Trusted IoT Connector”, developed by Fraunhofer AISEC allows for a secure usage of the Internet of Things even for critical processes. It ensures that only trustworthy and non-manipulated devices are used for crucial decisions. A secure execution environment, based on containers, enables the pre-processing of data by apps in the “Connector” itself. Through the enforcement of usage control, it is guaranteed that the data is only used for its designated purpose. In this way, new business models can securely be enabled within the Internet of Things.
Additional information: The Trusted Connector can be used to build secure embedded edge devices with or without hardware trust anchors, or as a cloud-based service for hosting demanding data analysis applications. It was designed with typical IIoT security requirements in mind, and offers a variety of features to protect data and ensure its integrity.
Example: The Trusted Connector could be used to secure a factory floor by ensuring that only trusted devices are allowed to connect to the network. It could also be used to protect sensitive data from unauthorized access, or to ensure that data is processed in compliance with regulations such as GDPR.
Publisher: Fraunhofer AISEC
Source: https://www.aisec.fraunhofer.de/content/dam/aisec/Dokumente/Flyer/Flyer_Trusted_IoT_Connector_engl.pdf

element.name: Data Integration
element.documentation:
Definition: Data Integration is the process of combining data from multiple sources into a unified and consistent view, enabling organizations to have a comprehensive understanding of their data. It involves extracting, transforming, and loading (ETL) data from various systems, databases, or files, and merging it into a single, coherent dataset.
Source: Techopedia
Source reference: https://www.techopedia.com/definition/1277/data-integration
Additional information: Data Integration plays a crucial role in enabling businesses to make informed decisions by providing a holistic view of their data. It eliminates data silos and ensures data consistency, accuracy, and reliability. The process involves identifying relevant data sources, mapping data elements, applying data transformations, and resolving any inconsistencies or conflicts. Data Integration can be achieved through various methods like manual coding, middleware tools, or specialized data integration platforms.
Example: An example of data integration is a retail company that combines data from its point-of-sale systems, customer relationship management (CRM) software, and inventory management system. By integrating this data, the company can gain insights into customer buying patterns, optimize inventory levels, and personalize marketing campaigns based on customer preferences.

element.name: e-Seal Creation
element.documentation:
Definition: e-Seal Creation ABB is an Application Service that enables to sign of data in electronic forms on behalf of a legal person
Source: eIDAS - REGULATION (EU) No 910/2014 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 23 July 2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market and repealing Directive 1999/93/EC.
Source reference: http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=uriserv%3AOJ.L_.2014.257.01.0073.01.ENG
Additional information: An ‘electronic seal' means data in electronic form, which is attached to or logically associated with other data in electronic form to ensure the latter’s origin and integrity. The ‘creator of a seal’ is a legal person who creates an electronic seal.
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): CEF eSignature DSS - DSS (Digital Signature Services) is an open-source software library for electronic signature creation and validation. DSS supports the creation and verification of interoperable and secure electronic signatures in line with European legislation. In particular, DSS aims to follow the eIDAS Regulation and related standards closely. DSS can be re-used in an IT solution for electronic signatures to ensure that signatures are created and verified in line with European legislation and standards. DSS allows re-use in a variety of different ways: in an applet, in a stand-alone application or in a server application. DSS can also be used as a reference implementation for IT solutions which do not directly re-use it. CEF eSignature's DSS open-source library delivers the following benefits to its users: • Open-source software under LGPL 2.1, a non-viral open source license; • Interoperability of the e-signatures; • Supports both e-signatures and e-seals; • Validation of countersignatures and multiple signatures; • Alignment with the eIDAS Regulation and related standards; • Supports EU standards on: o Signature formats and packaging methods; o Signature validation procedures; • Validation relying on Member States' trusted lists: o Status of trust service providers/trust service, compensation of information, path validation. https://ec.europa.eu/cefdigital/wiki/display/CEFDIGITAL/eSignaturefile:///C:/Users/bocquilp/Downloads/DSS(ServiceOfferingDescription)%20(v0.03)%20(5).pdf
IoP Dimension: Behavioral IoP
LOST view: Technical view - application

element.name: Identity Management
element.documentation:
Definition: Identity Management ABB is an Application Service that enables the set of processes, policies and technologies used to manage and secure digital entities of individuals, devices and applications.
Source: Inspired in eIDAS
Source reference: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32014R0910&from=EN
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): EU Login - EU Login is the European Commission's user authentication service. It allows authorised users to access a wide range of Commission web services. EU Login is the entry gate to sign in to different European Commission services and/or other systems. EU Login verifies your identity and allows recovering your personal settings, history and access rights in a secure way. You can sign in using social media accounts or the EU Login account. EU Login supports a variety of verification methods: • Password; • ECAS Mobile App PIN code; • ECAS Mobile App QR code; • On mobile authentication; • Mobile phone + SMS; • Token and Token CRAM. https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/cas/manuals/EU_Login_Tutorial_1.1.pdf

This can ensure and enhance the quality of data meant to be exchanged through interoperable systems, applications and digital public services.

property.value: A Contact Management Digital Service is a software solution designed to store, organize, and manage contact information for individuals and organizations. It facilitates the collection, tracking, and utilization of contact details, communication preferences, and interaction history to enhance communication and relationship management.

Individuals using a contact management app to keep track of friends, family, and professional contacts, syncing across multiple devices and integrating with social media platforms. A sales team using a CRM platform that includes contact management features to track interactions with potential clients, set reminders for follow-up, and record notes from meetings and calls. A nonprofit organization utilizing contact management software to manage donor information, send out newsletters, and organize fundraising events.

Contact Management Digital Services are essential tools for businesses and professionals who need to maintain a large network of contacts. These services often include features such as contact databases, search and filter capabilities, integration with email and calendar applications, task management, interaction tracking, and reporting functions. Advanced systems may also offer automation of communication processes, social media integration, and customer relationship management (CRM) features. The goal of contact management is to streamline the process of maintaining up-to-date contact information, improving the efficiency of communication, and fostering strong relationships with clients, customers, and partners.

element.name: Audit
element.documentation:
Definition: Audit ABB is an Application Service that enables the implementation of comprehensive procedural services capable of receiving inputs from different building blocks to ensure their correct behaviour, security or compliance with standards, regulations and best practices.

Source reference: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/simpl-cloud-edge-federations-and-data-spaces-made-simple
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): OpenIAM audit service - OpenIAM Auditing Service ensures that detailed information about events and activities associated with identities or resources are logged into a centralized repository and be tracked. It offers the following features: • Sign-on, Sign-off, • User: create, update, delete or disable accounts, • Role: create, update, delete or disable accounts, • Resource: create, update, delete or disable accounts, • Password changes, resets, challenge response questions changes, • Synchronization events, • Reconciliation events. Several reporting templates are provided for a BIRT report writer for use in an Eclipse designer. Organizations can also generate their own reports in BIRT with SQL. https://www.openiam.com/products/identity-manager/features/audit-compliance/
IoP Dimension: Behavioral IoP
LOST view: Technical view - application
Interoperability saliency: The Audit Service ABB is salient for technical interoperability because it defines the elements of an information system which need to be traced, for example to assure traceability of user actions as stated in the EIF: "Public administrations should ensure that a 'data access and authorisation plan’ which determines who has access to what data and under what conditions, to ensure privacy. Unauthorised access and security breaches should be monitored and appropriate actions should be taken to prevent any recurrence of breaches"

element.name: Tax virtual assistant service
element.documentation:
Definition: Tax Virtual Assistant Service refers to the utilization of features provided by a virtual assistance service that enables the use of virtual assistants to provide professional administrative, technical, or creative (social) assistance to customers remotely from a home office. These services are specifically tailored to handle tax-related tasks and queries.
Source: OpenAI
Source reference: https://www.openai.com/
Additional information: Tax Virtual Assistant Service is a modern approach to handling tax-related tasks and queries. It leverages the power of artificial intelligence to provide remote assistance to customers. These virtual assistants are programmed to handle a wide range of tasks including but not limited to tax preparation, tax advice, tax filing, and tax planning. They are capable of performing these tasks with high accuracy and efficiency, thus saving time and resources for both businesses and individuals. The use of such services is becoming increasingly popular due to the convenience and flexibility they offer. Customers can access these services from the comfort of their homes or offices, at any time of the day.
Example: 1. An individual uses a Tax Virtual Assistant Service to get assistance with their tax preparation. The virtual assistant helps them gather all the necessary documents, fill out the tax forms, and file them with the tax authorities. 2. A small business owner uses a Tax Virtual Assistant Service to get advice on tax planning. The virtual assistant provides them with strategies to minimize their tax liability and maximize their tax savings. 3. A large corporation uses a Tax Virtual Assistant Service to handle all their tax-related tasks. The virtual assistant takes care of everything from tax preparation to tax filing, allowing the corporation to focus on their core business activities.

element.name: Apache Kafka
element.documentation:
Description: Apache Kafka is an open-source distributed event streaming platform that is designed to handle high-throughput, fault-tolerant, and scalable real-time data streaming. It provides a publish-subscribe model where producers publish data to topics, and consumers subscribe to those topics to receive the data. Kafka stores the data in a fault-tolerant and durable manner, allowing it to be processed and consumed by multiple applications and systems.
Additional information: Apache Kafka is widely used in modern data architectures as a messaging system, enabling real-time data integration, streaming analytics, and event-driven architectures. It is built to handle massive amounts of data and provides low-latency, high-throughput, and fault-tolerant data streaming capabilities. Kafka's distributed nature allows it to scale horizontally across multiple servers, ensuring high availability and reliability. It provides strong durability guarantees by persisting data to disk, making it suitable for mission-critical applications. Kafka's flexible architecture allows seamless integration with various data systems, making it a popular choice for building data pipelines and streaming applications.
Example: One example of Apache Kafka's application is in a real-time analytics platform. Multiple data sources, such as web servers, mobile apps, and IoT devices, can publish events to Kafka topics. These events can then be consumed by analytics applications in real-time, allowing businesses to gain insights and make data-driven decisions instantly. Another example is its use in building scalable microservices architectures, where Kafka acts as a reliable communication layer between different microservices, ensuring data consistency and fault tolerance.
Publisher: Confluent
Source: https://www.confluent.io/what-is-apache-kafka/

property.value: A Knowledge Exchange Digital Service is an online platform that facilitates the sharing of information, expertise, and insights among individuals, organizations, or communities. It often includes features such as forums, document repositories, collaborative workspaces, and social networking capabilities to enhance communication and collaboration.

A university may use a Knowledge Exchange Digital Service to connect researchers across different disciplines, allowing them to share data, research findings, and methodologies, which can lead to interdisciplinary collaborations and advancements in research. A digital platform for healthcare professionals where they can exchange clinical case studies, best practices, and the latest research findings to improve patient care and stay updated with medical advancements. A government-initiated service that allows policymakers, experts, and stakeholders to discuss and refine policy proposals, share empirical evidence, and access a repository of historical policy documents and their outcomes.

The Knowledge Exchange Digital Service is designed to support the dissemination and collaborative use of knowledge across various domains. It can be tailored to specific industries or areas of interest, such as academia, healthcare, technology, or government. The service typically includes mechanisms for content management, user authentication, and access control to ensure that information is shared securely and with the appropriate audience. Advanced services may incorporate artificial intelligence and machine learning to curate and recommend content to users based on their interests and past interactions. The goal of such a service is to foster innovation, improve decision-making, and enable users to learn from each other's experiences and expertise.

Definition: A Knowledge Management Application Service is a software application or service that supports the processes of capturing, organizing, storing, retrieving, and sharing knowledge within an organization. It provides functionalities and tools to facilitate knowledge creation, acquisition, categorization, search, collaboration, and dissemination. The Knowledge Management Application Service typically includes features such as knowledge repositories, document management, collaboration platforms, content categorization, search capabilities, expertise location, and best practice sharing. It enables employees or users to access and leverage the organization's knowledge assets effectively, fostering innovation, decision-making, and continuous learning.

element.name: Tax coding system management
element.documentation:
Definition: Tax Coding System Management refers to the utilization or consumption of a coding system that enables the management of all detailed rules that individuals and businesses must adhere to when remitting a portion of their incomes to the federal or state government.
Source: Assistant's Knowledge
Source reference: N/A
Additional information: Tax Coding System Management is a crucial aspect of financial management for both individuals and businesses. It involves understanding and applying the complex rules and regulations set forth by the government regarding income tax. This system is designed to ensure that all taxpayers are compliant with the law and are paying the correct amount of tax. It involves various elements such as tax brackets, deductions, credits, and exemptions. Effective management of this system can help in avoiding penalties and ensuring smooth financial operations.
Example: Examples of Tax Coding System Management include the use of software or online platforms that help individuals and businesses calculate their taxes based on their income and expenses. These tools often include features that allow users to input their financial information and automatically calculate the amount of tax they owe. They also often include features that help users understand and apply the various tax rules and regulations that apply to them.

It provides tools and features such as video conferencing, instant messaging, document sharing, and virtual whiteboards to support real-time or asynchronous interactions. property.value: Digital collaboration refers to the use of digital tools and platforms to work together with others in a virtual environment. It involves the sharing of information, ideas, and resources to achieve common goals or complete tasks, regardless of the physical location of the participants.

Using Zoom or Microsoft Teams to hold virtual meetings with team members located in different cities or countries. Utilizing Google Docs or Microsoft OneDrive to collaboratively edit documents in real-time, allowing multiple users to make changes simultaneously. Employing tools like Asana, Trello, or Jira to track project progress, assign tasks, and manage deadlines across a team. Leveraging Slack or Microsoft Teams for quick communication and to facilitate discussions in dedicated channels for different topics or projects. Using Office 365 or G Suite to access a comprehensive set of tools that support various aspects of collaboration, including email, calendaring, file storage, and more.

Digital collaboration encompasses a wide range of technologies and practices, including but not limited to, video conferencing, cloud-based document and file sharing, project management applications, instant messaging, and collaborative software suites that integrate multiple functions. These tools enable individuals and teams to communicate in real-time or asynchronously, enhancing productivity and facilitating the exchange of knowledge. Effective digital collaboration requires not only the right tools but also a culture that promotes open communication, trust, and the willingness to share expertise. As remote work and distributed teams become more prevalent, digital collaboration is increasingly critical for maintaining team cohesion and ensuring successful project outcomes.

element.name: Tax customer messaging solution
element.documentation:
Definition: A Tax Customer Messaging Solution refers to the use or consumption of features provided by a customer messaging solution that enables remote interaction with the customer through various messaging platforms. This solution is often used in the tax industry to facilitate communication between tax professionals and their clients.
Source: Assistant's Knowledge
Source reference: N/A
Additional information: The Tax Customer Messaging Solution is a crucial tool in today's digital age, especially in the tax industry. It allows tax professionals to interact with their clients remotely, providing a platform for discussions, clarifications, and updates regarding tax-related matters. This solution may include features such as automated responses, personalized messages, real-time communication, and more. It can be integrated into various messaging platforms, making it a versatile and flexible tool for enhancing customer service and engagement. Moreover, it can also help in improving the efficiency and productivity of tax professionals by streamlining the communication process.
Example: 1. A tax professional using a Tax Customer Messaging Solution to send automated reminders to their clients about upcoming tax deadlines. 2. A tax firm integrating this solution into their system to provide real-time responses to client inquiries regarding their tax returns. 3. A tax consultant using this solution to send personalized messages to their clients, providing them with updates and advice on their tax situation.

element.name: Content Management
element.documentation:
Definition: Content Management ABB is an Application Service to enable the procedures to create, manage, and publish digital content, such as text, images, videos, and documents
Source: EUI
Source reference: https://www.eui.eu/ServicesAndAdmin/CommunicationsService/WebUnit/Web-CMS
Additional information: Content Management ABB is an Application Service being responsible for: - developing Website templates and functionalities; - assigning appropriate user permissions and workflows; - providing trainings to the web working group; - developing tools and web controls to speed up and facilitate the work of the web working group; - giving support and advice to the web working group; - ensuring continuity of service and performance; - ensuring security and accessibility on the website; - ensuring disaster recovery processes and backup procedures; - setting up the website information architecture within the CMS; - setting up alert procedures and analytics on usage of the platform.
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): FPFIS-CMS: "The European Commission announced in the Commission Internet strategy plans to transform the EUROPA web site from a source of one-way information into a tool for communication and interaction (i.e. provide modern interactive web sites for the citizens and stakeholders). Web sites are a key tool for external communications. They are the institution's business card. Websites are a very cost-effective and efficient means of communication. EUROPA now hosts over 460 websites. EUROPA would benefit from fewer and better sites to respond to user needs. To address the shortcomings, as part of the Commission's IT governance process, the College on 30 November 2011, instructed Commission departments to rationalise the Institution's web presence. Reduce the cost (human, financial, technical) of the Commission's web presence via exploiting economies of scale and eliminating redundancies by building corporate solutions. The European Commission should offer a corporate service which optimizes and harmonizes the use of different website tools, which speeds up the creation of new external dynamic and social websites (i.e. in days or weeks and not months) and which provides a common solid modern shared infrastructure to support the rapid deployment of these sites". https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/fpfis/mwikis/thinktank/index.php/Content_Management_System_of_the_Flexible_Platform
IoP Dimension: Behavioral IoP
LOST view: Technical view - application

element.name: Archival Information Packages
element.documentation:
Definition: Archival Information Packages (AIPs) refer to standardized packages of digital content and associated metadata that are created for long-term preservation and access in the context of eArchiving. AIPs encapsulate the essential components of digital objects, including their content, structure, and contextual information, ensuring their authenticity, integrity, and usability over time. AIPs typically adhere to established archival standards and formats, facilitating interoperability and long-term preservation strategies. The service of managing AIPs involves activities such as ingestion, storage, metadata management, preservation planning, and retrieval.
Source: OASIS

element.name: Service Metadata Locator
element.documentation:
LOST view: TVA-Functional Architecture Principles
Identifier: http://data.europa.eu/dr8/egovera/ServiceMetadataLocatorApplicationService
EIRA traceability: eira:DigitalSolutionApplicationService
ABB name: egovera:ServiceMetadataLocatorApplicationService
EIRA concept: eira:ArchitectureBuildingBlock
Last modification: 2022-18-01

property.value: A Service Metadata Locator is a digital service that enables the discovery and retrieval of metadata about other services within a distributed system or across the internet.

Web Services Discovery In a web services environment, a Service Metadata Locator can be used to store and provide access to WSDL (Web Services Description Language) files. Clients can query the locator to find the appropriate WSDL for a web service they wish to consume, enabling them to dynamically generate client stubs and interact with the service.
Microservices Architecture In a microservices architecture, a Service Metadata Locator can be used by individual microservices to register their availability and by others to discover these services. For example, when a new microservice is deployed, it registers its metadata with the locator. Other microservices or service gateways can query the locator to route requests or compose services.

The Service Metadata Locator is a crucial component in service-oriented architectures (SOA) and microservices architectures, where services are loosely coupled and can be dynamically discovered and integrated. It acts as a directory or registry that holds information about the services available within a system, such as service endpoints, interfaces, protocols, and policies. This information is essential for service consumers to understand how to interact with the services. The locator often provides an API or interface through which services can register their metadata and through which consumers can query for services that meet certain criteria. This enables automation in service discovery and integration, which is vital for scalability and flexibility in complex systems.

element.name: Authentication
element.documentation:
Definition: Authentication ABB is an Application Service that enables the functionality of grating users to access the platforms or the services.
Source: eIDAS - REGULATION (EU) No 910/2014 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 23 July 2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market and repealing Directive 1999/93/EC.
Source reference: http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=uriserv%3AOJ.L_.2014.257.01.0073.01.ENG
Additional information: ‘Electronic identification’ means the process of using person identification data in electronic form uniquely representing either a natural or legal person, or a natural person representing a legal person; ‘Authentication’ means an electronic process that enables the electronic identification of a natural or legal person, or the origin and integrity of data in electronic form to be confirmed;
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): EU Login - EU Login is the European Commission's user authentication service. It allows authorised users to access a wide range of Commission web services. EU Login is the entry gate to sign in to different European Commission services and/or other systems. EU Login verifies your identity and allows recovering your personal settings, history and access rights in a secure way. You can sign in using social media accounts or the EU Login account. EU Login supports a variety of verification methods: • Password; • ECAS Mobile App PIN code; • ECAS Mobile App QR code; • On mobile authentication; • Mobile phone + SMS; • Token and Token CRAM. https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/cas/about.html

element.name: Red Hat OpenShift
element.documentation:
Description: Red Hat OpenShift is a container application platform that enables developers to build, deploy, and manage applications across various cloud environments. It provides a consistent and secure foundation for developing and scaling applications, allowing teams to focus on delivering value rather than managing infrastructure. OpenShift utilizes Kubernetes orchestration to automate the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications.
Additional information: Red Hat OpenShift simplifies the process of developing, deploying, and scaling applications by providing a comprehensive platform that abstracts away the underlying infrastructure complexities. It offers a self-service environment for developers to easily create and deploy applications using containers, which encapsulate the application and its dependencies. OpenShift provides features like automated scaling, load balancing, and continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, enabling teams to rapidly iterate and deliver software. It also offers built-in security features, such as role-based access control (RBAC) and image scanning, to ensure the integrity and compliance of applications. With its support for multiple cloud providers and on-premises environments, OpenShift offers flexibility and portability for applications across different infrastructures.
Example: An example of using Red Hat OpenShift is a development team building a microservices-based application. They can leverage OpenShift to create and manage containers for each microservice, allowing independent development and scaling of individual components. OpenShift's built-in CI/CD capabilities enable automated testing and deployment of new versions, ensuring a streamlined development process. The team can easily scale the application horizontally by adding more container instances as needed, and OpenShift's load balancing features distribute the traffic efficiently. With OpenShift's portability, the team can seamlessly deploy the application across different cloud providers or on-premises environments, adapting to changing business needs.
Publisher: Red Hat
Source: https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/cloud-computing/openshift

element.name: Conformance Testing
element.documentation:
Definition: Conformance Testing ABB is an Application Service that enables the activities and rules to determine whether a tool, platform or service faithfully meets the requirements of a standard or specification
Source: NIST
Source reference: https://www.nist.gov/itl/ssd/information-systems-group/conformance-testing
Additional information: The logistics of interoperability testing is usually more costly (time, coordination, interoperability), and interoperability testing is no substitute for a conformance test suite. Experience shows that interoperability testing is more successful and less costly when conformance of implementations has been tested first.
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): Interoperability Testbed - The Test Bed allows users to execute predefined test cases on their systems in order to test the conformance to standards and requirements, simulate a web-service, validate content and test a complete message exchange protocol. The Testbed manages test cases and users, and orchestrates domain-specific components, the domain-specific logic is in separate components that are used via web services. Test results are provided in a standardised, machine-readable format. The Test Bed also offers a test registry and repository (TRR) to store test artefacts (assertions, test cases, validation schemas, etc.) and compile test services (validation services, simulator services, etc.). Please visit the following website for more information: https://ec.europa.eu/isa2/solutions/interoperability-test-bed_en
IoP Dimension: Behavioral IoP
LOST view: Technical view - Infrastructure
Interoperability saliency: The Conformance Testing Services ABB is salient for technical interoperability because it enables the validation and verification that several solutions at one or more layers of the interoperability stack and they satisfy certain interoperability requirements.

element.name: Transaction network analysis
element.documentation:
Description: Transaction Network Analysis is an anti-VAT fraud tool from the European Commission that enables Member States to swiftly exchange and collectively process VAT data. This leads to the early detection of suspicious networks.
Additional information: Transaction Network Analysis is a sophisticated tool designed to combat VAT fraud within the European Union. It allows for the rapid exchange and joint processing of VAT data between Member States. This tool is particularly useful in identifying and detecting suspicious networks that may be involved in fraudulent activities. By using this tool, Member States can more effectively monitor VAT transactions, identify potential fraud, and take appropriate action in a timely manner. The tool is part of the European Commission's broader efforts to strengthen the EU's VAT system and combat fraud.
Example: For instance, if a company in one Member State is suspected of fraudulent VAT activities, the Transaction Network Analysis tool can be used to quickly share this information with other Member States. This allows for a coordinated response and the potential to halt the fraudulent activities before they cause significant damage. Similarly, the tool can be used to identify patterns of suspicious activity across multiple Member States, providing a more comprehensive picture of VAT fraud within the EU.
Publisher: European Commission
Source: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/business/vat/action-plan-vat/single-vat-area_en

element.name: OpenPeppol
element.documentation:
Description: OpenPeppol is a non-profit international association that manages the development and maintenance of the PEPPOL Network. PEPPOL is a set of standards for exchanging electronic business documents, such as invoices, orders, and delivery notes. The PEPPOL Network is a global network of organizations that provide access to PEPPOL services.
Additional information: OpenPeppol is a non-profit organization that oversees the PEPPOL network, a global network that allows organizations to exchange business documents electronically. The PEPPOL network is based on a set of standards that facilitate the exchange of documents such as invoices, orders, and delivery notes. OpenPeppol's role is to manage the development and maintenance of this network, ensuring its smooth operation and continuous improvement.
Example: A company can use the PEPPOL network to send an electronic invoice to a customer in another country. The invoice is sent through the network, which ensures that it is delivered in a format that the customer's system can process. This eliminates the need for manual data entry and reduces the risk of errors. Similarly, a supplier can send an electronic delivery note to a customer, who can then automatically update their inventory management system.

Source: https://peppol.eu/
