dct:title: Business Agnostic Ontology Solutions

property.value: Business Agnostic Ontology Solutions (BAOS) is a grouping that covers a range of standardized representations and frameworks for describing, modeling, validating, and interchanging data and metadata in various contexts. These solutions are designed to facilitate semantic interoperability, data discoverability, and the description of organizational structures, roles, relationships, and digital assets, particularly in the field of Linked Data and the Semantic Web.

For example, the W3C Organization Ontology can be used to model the hierarchy, departments, employees, and roles of an organization in a standardized way. The SHACL can be used to validate the structure and constraints of RDF graphs. The PROV-O can be used to represent and interchange provenance information generated in different systems. The FOAF project can be used to create machine-readable Web homepages for people, groups, companies, and other kinds of things. The DCAT-AP can be used to provide semantic interoperability for data portals in Europe. The ADMS and ADMS-AP can be used to facilitate the description and discovery of digital assets in the context of public administration. The DCAT can be used to describe datasets and data services in a catalog. The ODRL can be used to describe and model various aspects of organizations.

The elements of BAOS include W3C Organization, W3C Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL), PROV-O, FOAF, DCAT-AP, ADMS, ADMS-AP, DCAT, and ODRL. These elements provide a set of classes, properties, and restrictions that can be used to represent and interchange provenance information generated in different systems and under different contexts. They also provide a language and framework for describing and validating the structure and constraints of RDF graphs, a collection of basic terms for machine-readable Web homepages, and a specification for metadata records to meet the specific application needs of data portals in Europe.

element.name: European Binding Instruments
element.documentation:
Definition: European Binding Instruments (EBI) is a grouping that covers a wide range of legislative and regulatory instruments enacted by the European Union (EU) to govern various aspects of interoperability within the digital single market. These instruments aim to harmonize rules and regulations across EU member states, promote fair competition and innovation, protect consumer rights, and ensure the security and privacy of electronic transactions. The EBI includes directives, regulations, and proposals that address issues related to governance, behavioural, and structural interoperability.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The European Binding Instruments (EBI) catalogue includes a variety of legislative and regulatory instruments that govern different aspects of interoperability within the digital single market of the European Union. These instruments are grouped into three categories: Legislation on Governance Interoperability, Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability, and Legislation on Structural Interoperability. Each category includes a number of specific instruments, such as directives and regulations, that address specific issues related to electronic communications, digital content and services, public procurement, insurance distribution, payment services, cross-border parcel delivery services, geo-blocking, electronic commerce, open data, data protection, free flow of non-personal data, web accessibility, electronic invoicing, cybersecurity, and electronic identification and trust services.
Example: An example of a European Binding Instrument is the Directive (EU) 2018/1972, also known as the European Electronic Communications Code. This directive aims to modernize and harmonize the regulatory framework for electronic communications across the European Union. It sets out rules and obligations for electronic communications services, networks, and infrastructure providers, with the goal of promoting competition, investment, and innovation in the sector. Another example is the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which is a regulation enacted by the European Union in 2016 to protect the privacy and personal data of individuals within the EU. It establishes rules and guidelines for the processing of personal data by organizations, including the collection, storage, and transfer of such data.

element.name: Information Architect Concerns
element.documentation:
Definition: Information Architect Concerns ABB is a Grouping that covers the processes an information architect should follow, and the relation/influence of process related with other roles' processes, to read/assess/understand an eGovERA model. It includes elements such as 'Semantic view' and 'Organisational view'.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Information Architect Concerns ABB is a crucial component in the eGovERA model, providing a structured approach for information architects to understand and assess the model. It includes elements like 'Semantic view', which refers to the process of understanding the meaning and interpretation of the information in the model, and 'Organisational view', which refers to the process of understanding the organizational structure and roles in the model. These elements help the information architect to understand the model from different perspectives and to ensure that the model is accurately interpreted and implemented.
Example: For instance, an information architect might start by examining the 'Semantic view' to understand the meaning of the information in the eGovERA model. They might then move on to the 'Organisational view' to understand how the roles and responsibilities are distributed in the model. This comprehensive approach ensures that the architect has a thorough understanding of the model and can effectively guide its implementation.

element.name: Business Agnostic Metadata Catalogue Solutions
element.documentation:
Definition: NARRATIVE:The 'Business Agnostic Metadata Catalogue' in ArchiMate is a grouping that organizes various elements based on their concerns or responsibilities. In the provided JSON, there are three main elements: [JRC Data Catalogue], [SV-Metadata Catalogue], and [Smart Data Models]. 1. [JRC Data Catalogue]: This is a Data Object SBB type element. It represents the Joint Research Center (JRC) Data Catalogue, which is a collection of metadata records providing information about datasets produced by the JRC. The JRC, as the European Commission's in-house science service, conducts research to provide independent scientific advice and support to the policies of the European Union. This element does not contain any sub-elements.2. [SV-Metadata Catalogue]: This is an Archimate Diagram-model ABB type element. The description is not provided in the JSON, but based on its type, it can be inferred that this element represents a metadata catalogue in the form of an ArchiMate diagram model. This element also does not contain any sub-elements.3. [Smart Data Models]: This is another Data Object SBB type element. It represents a smart data model, which includes three elements: the schema (technical representation of the model defining the technical data types and structure), the specification (a written document for human readers), and the examples of the payloads for NGSIv2 and NGSI-LD versions. This element also does not contain any sub-elements.In the context of ArchiMate's grouping, these elements are catalogued in the 'Business Agnostic Metadata Catalogue' based on their responsibilities or concerns, which revolve around data and metadata management, research, and policy support.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The BAMS catalogue includes the JRC Data Catalogue, a collection of metadata records detailing datasets produced by the Joint Research Centre (JRC) in line with its Data Policy. The JRC, the European Commission's in-house science service, conducts research to provide independent scientific advice and support to EU policies. Another key element in the catalogue is Smart Data Models. These models include a schema (technical representation of the model defining the technical data types and structure), a specification (written document for human readers), and examples of the payloads for NGSIv2 and NGSI-LD versions. These models are 'smart' because they are designed to be easily understood and used by both humans and machines, facilitating more effective data management and utilization.
Example: An example of the application of the JRC Data Catalogue could be a research institution using the catalogue to access and utilize JRC's datasets for a study on EU policy impact. Similarly, a tech company could use the Smart Data Models in the development of a new software product, leveraging the models to ensure that their data is structured and managed in a standardized, efficient manner.

element.name: Observability Requirements Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Observability Requirements Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers non-functional requirements related to system monitoring, logging, and tiered levels of support. These requirements are critical for ensuring the reliability, availability, performance, security, and effective use of IT systems and applications.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Observability Requirements Catalogue ABB includes three main elements: Alerts and Monitoring, Logging, and Tiered Levels of Support. Alerts and Monitoring refer to the system's ability to detect and report issues or anomalies in real-time, ensuring optimal performance and availability. Logging involves recording events and activities within a system or application, providing a detailed record of system behavior for troubleshooting, auditing, and analysis. Tiered Levels of Support refers to the hierarchical provision of technical support to users based on their needs, ensuring quick and efficient resolution of technical issues. These requirements are essential for maintaining the security and reliability of IT systems, meeting regulatory compliance requirements, minimizing downtime, and enabling effective use of the system or application.
Example: Examples of application for the Observability Requirements Catalogue ABB include: a cloud-based software application implementing real-time alerts and monitoring to detect and report system errors, a banking system implementing logging to record user actions and system errors for auditing and analysis, and a customer support center implementing tiered levels of support to provide appropriate technical assistance to users based on their needs.

element.name: Governance Analyst Concerns
element.documentation:
Definition: Governance Analyst Concerns ABB is a Grouping that covers the processes a governance analyst should follow, and the relation/influence of process related with other roles' processes, to read/assess/understand an eGovERA model. It includes elements such as the Organisational view and Legal view.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Governance Analyst Concerns ABB is a comprehensive catalogue of elements that a governance analyst needs to consider when assessing an eGovERA model. It includes the Organisational view, which pertains to the understanding of the structure, roles, and responsibilities within the organization. The Legal view, on the other hand, deals with the legal aspects, regulations, and compliance requirements that the organization needs to adhere to. These elements are crucial in providing a holistic understanding of the eGovERA model and its implications on the organization's governance.
Example: For instance, a governance analyst may use the Organisational view to understand the hierarchy within the organization, the roles of different stakeholders, and how decisions are made and implemented. In the Legal view, the analyst may assess the legal compliance of the organization, understanding the laws and regulations it needs to follow, and ensuring that the organization's processes are in line with these legal requirements.

element.name: Business Agnostic Data Space Digital Public Services Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic Data Space Digital Public Services Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a range of digital public services that are not specific to any business sector. These services include eSignature, eNotification, Log Management, Audit, eIdentification, Digital Collaboration and a sub-catalogue of services for Business Agnostic Data Space Participants.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The catalogue is a comprehensive collection of digital public services that are designed to be applicable across various business sectors. These services include eSignature, which provides digital signature services; eNotification, which provides digital notification services; Log Management, which provides digital log management services; Audit, which provides digital audit services; eIdentification, which provides digital identification services; and Digital Collaboration, which provides digital collaboration services. The catalogue also includes a sub-catalogue of services specifically for Business Agnostic Data Space Participants, which includes services such as Data Extraction, Transformation and Loading; Content Management; Open Data Management; Workflow Management; Data Exchange; eArchiving; Anonymisation; and Secure Access Control.
Example: For instance, a business in the healthcare sector could use the eSignature service to digitally sign documents, the eNotification service to send digital notifications to patients, the Log Management service to manage digital logs of patient records, the Audit service to conduct digital audits of their operations, the eIdentification service to digitally identify patients, and the Digital Collaboration service to collaborate digitally with other healthcare providers. They could also use the services in the Business Agnostic Data Space Participant sub-catalogue to manage their data and workflows.

element.name: Business Agnostic Conformance Solutions
element.documentation:
Description: Bussiness Agnostic Conformance Solutions ABB is a grouping that refers to actual solutions that facilitate the alignment of business processes, regardless of the industry or sector, with the necessary regulatory and compliance requirements. These solutions are designed to be adaptable and flexible, allowing businesses from different sectors to conform to the same set of standards or regulations.
Additional information: These solutions are typically software or digital services that provide tools and features to help businesses manage and monitor their compliance with various regulations. They may include features for risk management, audit trails, reporting, and more. The 'agnostic' aspect refers to the fact that these solutions are not tied to any specific business or industry - they can be used by any type of business that needs to comply with certain regulations. This makes them highly versatile and useful for businesses operating in highly regulated industries, such as finance, healthcare, and more.
Example: Examples of Business Agnostic Conformance Solutions could include compliance management software like LogicGate or Onspring. These platforms provide tools for risk management, compliance, audit management, and more, and can be used by businesses in any industry. Another example could be a digital service that provides a platform for businesses to manage and monitor their GDPR compliance, which would be applicable to any business that handles personal data of EU citizens.
Publisher: EIRA Team Research

element.name: Security Requirements Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Security Requirements Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a range of non-functional IT requirements that are critical for ensuring the security, integrity, and reliability of a system or application. These requirements include confidentiality, integrity, nonrepudiation, accountability, authenticity, auditability, authentication, authorization, legality, compliance, and privacy. Each of these elements plays a crucial role in protecting sensitive information, preventing unauthorized access or modification, ensuring compliance with laws and regulations, and maintaining the trustworthiness and credibility of the system.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Security Requirements Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of IT security requirements that are essential for any system or application that handles sensitive data. These requirements are designed to protect the data from unauthorized access, ensure its accuracy and consistency, provide proof of transactions, track user activities, verify user identities, grant appropriate access levels, comply with legal and regulatory standards, and safeguard privacy. Failure to meet these requirements can result in security breaches, loss of data integrity, legal penalties, and loss of trust among users and stakeholders.
Example: For example, a healthcare application would need to meet the requirements of confidentiality to protect patient data, integrity to ensure the accuracy of medical records, nonrepudiation to provide proof of medical orders, accountability to track user activities, authenticity to verify the genuineness of data, auditability to provide a record of transactions, authentication to verify user identities, authorization to grant appropriate access levels, legality to comply with healthcare regulations, compliance to adhere to data protection standards, and privacy to safeguard patient privacy.

For example, a healthcare application would need to meet the requirements of confidentiality to protect patient data, integrity to ensure the accuracy of medical records, nonrepudiation to provide proof of medical orders, accountability to track user activities, authenticity to verify the genuineness of data, auditability to provide a record of transactions, authentication to verify user identities, authorization to grant appropriate access levels, legality to comply with healthcare regulations, compliance to adhere to data protection standards, and privacy to safeguard patient privacy.

The Security Requirements Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of IT security requirements that are essential for any system or application that handles sensitive data. These requirements are designed to protect the data from unauthorized access, ensure its accuracy and consistency, provide proof of transactions, track user activities, verify user identities, grant appropriate access levels, comply with legal and regulatory standards, and safeguard privacy. Failure to meet these requirements can result in security breaches, loss of data integrity, legal penalties, and loss of trust among users and stakeholders.

element.name: Tax Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Tax Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NBI) is a grouping that covers a wide range of elements related to national tax legislation, schemas, and acts. These elements encompass various aspects of tax law, including tributary court cases, income-related taxes, mobile assets, carbon-related taxes, company classification rules, deductible taxes on loans and mortgages, taxes related to property, religious community fees, criminal assets, social tax, tax fraud and evasion, unemployment insurance, VAT, tax procedures, and property tax.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The elements within the Tax Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NBI) catalogue are designed to provide a comprehensive overview of national tax legislation and related schemas. They cover a broad spectrum of tax-related topics, from specific types of taxes (income, property, VAT, etc.) to legal procedures and strategies for combating tax fraud. Each element represents a distinct aspect of tax law, providing a detailed picture of the tax landscape and facilitating interoperability in governance.
Example: For instance, the 'National Schema on tributary court cases' element would contain information about the legal framework and procedures for handling tax-related court cases at the national level. Similarly, the 'National Schema on Co2 (carbon) related taxes' would detail the legislation and regulations surrounding carbon taxation. The 'Legislation on the deductible tax es on loans and mortgages' would provide information on how these types of taxes can be deducted under national law.

element.name: Business Agnostic Organisational Governance Frameworks Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Organisational Governance Frameworks Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a set of business objects that enable the protection, confidentiality, and interoperability of data, information, and knowledge assets and the organizational resources handling them. It includes the Security Framework, Privacy Framework, and Interoperability Framework.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Organisational Governance Frameworks Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of frameworks that are designed to guide organizations in managing and protecting their data and information assets. The Security Framework focuses on the protection of these assets and the resources handling them. The Privacy Framework, on the other hand, emphasizes the confidentiality aspects of these assets and resources. Lastly, the Interoperability Framework is designed to enable organizations to collaborate effectively towards the joint delivery of public services. It does this by specifying a set of common elements such as vocabulary, concepts, principles, guidelines, and recommendations.
Example: An example of the application of the Organisational Governance Frameworks Catalogue ABB could be a public service organization that needs to ensure the security and privacy of its data while also needing to collaborate with other organizations. The Security Framework would guide the organization in protecting its data and resources. The Privacy Framework would help ensure the confidentiality of the data. The Interoperability Framework would provide the necessary guidelines and recommendations for effective collaboration with other organizations.

element.name: Geo-spatial Data Format Solutions
element.documentation:
Definition: Geo-spatial Data Format is a grouping that covers various formats used for encoding, storing, and exchanging geospatial data. These formats include GeoJSON, KML, and GML, each of which serves a unique purpose and is used in different applications. They provide a standardized and flexible way to represent geographic features and their associated attributes, facilitating the exchange of geographic data between different systems and applications.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: GeoJSON is a format for encoding geospatial data in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), providing a standard and flexible way to represent geographic features, such as points, lines, and polygons, along with their associated attributes. Keyhole Markup Language (KML) is an XML notation for expressing geographic annotation and visualization within two-dimensional maps and three-dimensional Earth browsers, developed for use with Google Earth. Geography Markup Language (GML) is an XML-based format used to encode geographic information, including the geometry and properties of geographic features, facilitating the exchange of geographic data between different systems and applications.
Example: GeoJSON is often used in web applications that need to visualize geographic data, such as interactive maps. KML is commonly used to create and share geographic data with Google Earth and other Earth browsers. GML is used in a variety of domains, including geographic information systems (GIS), web mapping, and location-based services.

element.name: Business Agnostic Identity Management Solutions
element.documentation:
Description: Bussiness Agnostic Identity Management Solutions (BAIMS) is a grouping that refers to actual solutions that facilitate the management of user identities across various business models and industries. These solutions are designed to be flexible and adaptable, allowing businesses of any type or size to effectively manage user access, authentication, and security.
Additional information: BAIMS are crucial in today's digital age where security and privacy are of utmost importance. They provide a comprehensive approach to managing the identities of users in an organization, regardless of the nature of the business. They are designed to handle tasks such as user authentication, authorization, roles and access management, password management, policy enforcement, and audit and reporting. These solutions are not tied to a specific business model or industry, making them versatile and adaptable. They can be integrated with various systems and platforms, providing a seamless user experience while ensuring security and compliance.
Example: Examples of application of BAIMS include: 1) In a healthcare setting, these solutions can be used to manage the identities of doctors, nurses, and patients, ensuring that only authorized individuals have access to sensitive patient data. 2) In a retail business, they can be used to manage the identities of customers and employees, facilitating secure transactions and protecting customer information. 3) In a financial institution, they can be used to manage the identities of account holders and employees, ensuring secure access to financial data and systems.
Publisher: EIRA Team Research

element.name: Enterprise Architecture Framework (EAF) alignment guidelines
element.documentation:
Definition: Enterprise Architecture Framework (EAF) alignment guidelines ABB is a Grouping that covers the process of establishing a harmonious relationship between the European Interoperability Reference Architecture (EIRA) model and any given Enterprise Architecture Framework (EAF). The aim is to make the EIRA model fully compliant with the chosen EAF, promoting uniformity across the architectural ecosystem.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The EAF alignment guidelines serve as an integral part of the process, aiming to establish a harmonious relationship between the European Interoperability Reference Architecture (EIRA) model and any given Enterprise Architecture Framework (EAF). The ultimate goal is to make the EIRA model fully compliant with the chosen EAF, promoting uniformity across the architectural ecosystem. The elements contained within these guidelines include Interoperable European Solution, Achieve Interoperability, Creation of Interoperable European Solutions, European Interoperability Reference Architecture, Coordination Capacity, Regulatory Capacity, Delivery Capacity, Analytical Capacity, EIRA Ontology, Public Administration, Architecture Principle, Constraints, Assumptions and Decisions, Shared Legal Content, Shared Organisational Content, Digital Solution Requirement, Iternational Data Spaces Reference Architecture Model (IDS-RAM), Data Spaces Business Alliance, Eclipse Dataspace Components, JRC Data Spaces Knowledge Base, FIWARE for Data Spaces, Gaia-X Data Spaces Community.
Example: An example of the application of the EAF alignment guidelines could be the process of aligning a national public administration's enterprise architecture with the EIRA model. This would involve assessing the current architecture, identifying gaps and areas of non-compliance, and implementing changes to achieve alignment. The guidelines would provide a roadmap for this process, outlining the necessary steps and considerations.

element.name: Software Architect Data Spaces Concerns
element.documentation:
Definition: Software Architect Data Spaces Concerns ABB is a Grouping that covers the processes, roles, and relationships a software architect should follow to read, assess, and understand an eGovERA model for the purpose of understanding and developing a Data Spaces solution or architecture. It includes elements such as 'Technical view - application' and 'Semantic view'.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Software Architect Data Spaces Concerns ABB is a comprehensive catalogue of elements that a software architect needs to consider when working with an eGovERA model to develop a Data Spaces solution or architecture. It includes the 'Technical view - application', which refers to the technical aspects of the application, and the 'Semantic view', which refers to the meaning and interpretation of the data. These elements are crucial in understanding the model and developing an effective solution.
Example: For example, a software architect might need to understand the technical infrastructure of the application, such as the programming languages used, the database management systems in place, and the server architecture. For instance, the software architect might need to understand the semantics of the data, such as the meaning of different data fields, the relationships between different data entities, and the rules and constraints that govern the data.

element.name: Tax Datasets Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Tax Datasets Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a variety of metadata and catalogues related to taxation. It includes tax statistical metadata, public tax metadata, taxpayer behavior history metadata, business sector catalogue, and WTO trade and goods exchange metadata. These elements provide comprehensive information on different aspects of taxation, from public tax data to specific details about taxpayer behavior and international trade.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Tax Datasets Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of metadata and catalogues that provide detailed information on various aspects of taxation. The 'Tax statistical metadata' provides statistical data related to taxation. The 'Public tax metadata' provides information on public tax data. The 'Taxpayer behavior history metadata' provides information on the behavior of taxpayers over time. The 'Business Sector catalogue' provides a catalogue of different business sectors for reference. The 'WTO trade and goods exchange metadata' provides information on trade and goods exchange as per the World Trade Organization. Each of these elements plays a crucial role in understanding and analyzing taxation data.
Example: For instance, the 'Tax statistical metadata' can be used by researchers to analyze tax trends over time. The 'Public tax metadata' can be used by the public to understand the tax data released by the government. The 'Taxpayer behavior history metadata' can be used by tax authorities to understand taxpayer behavior and compliance. The 'Business Sector catalogue' can be used by businesses to identify their sector for tax purposes. The 'WTO trade and goods exchange metadata' can be used by international trade analysts to understand the impact of taxes on trade and goods exchange.

element.name: Tax Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NNBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Tax Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NNBI) ABB is a grouping that covers the legislative, regulatory, and policy elements that facilitate the interaction and cooperation between different governance systems in the context of tax legislation. It encompasses the rules, principles, and practices that enable the exchange of information and the alignment of procedures and processes between different tax governance systems.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The NNBI ABB is a comprehensive catalogue of elements that are crucial for ensuring the smooth interoperability of different tax governance systems. It includes, but is not limited to, laws, regulations, policies, procedures, guidelines, standards, and best practices. These elements are designed to facilitate the exchange of tax-related information, the alignment of tax procedures and processes, and the resolution of tax-related disputes between different governance systems. The NNBI ABB is used by tax authorities, policymakers, tax professionals, and other stakeholders to understand and navigate the complex landscape of tax governance interoperability.
Example: Examples of application of the NNBI ABB include the use of its elements to harmonize tax procedures between different countries, to facilitate the exchange of tax-related information between different tax authorities, to align the tax policies of different jurisdictions, and to resolve tax-related disputes in a fair, transparent, and efficient manner.

element.name: Usability Requirements Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Usability Requirements Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a range of non-functional IT requirements that are crucial for ensuring the usability and accessibility of a system or application. This includes requirements related to accessibility, learnability, and API contracts. Each of these elements plays a key role in ensuring that the system or application is user-friendly, inclusive, and efficient, and that it complies with relevant laws and regulations.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Usability Requirements Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of non-functional requirements that are essential for the development of user-friendly and accessible IT systems and applications. The catalogue includes 'Accessibility', which ensures that the system can be used by people with disabilities or impairments; 'Learnability', which measures how quickly and efficiently users can learn to use the system; and 'API contract', which specifies the rules and guidelines for how an API should behave. By adhering to these requirements, developers can create systems and applications that are inclusive, efficient, and compliant with relevant laws and regulations.
Example: For instance, when developing a new web application, a developer might refer to the Usability Requirements Catalogue ABB to ensure that the application is accessible to users with disabilities. This could involve implementing features such as screen readers, keyboard navigation, and alternative text for images. The developer might also use the catalogue to ensure that the application is easy to learn and use, by creating clear and intuitive interfaces and providing well-organized documentation and help resources. Finally, the developer might refer to the 'API contract' requirement to ensure that the application's API is consistent, predictable, and easy to integrate with other systems.

The catalogue includes 'Accessibility', which ensures that the system can be used by people with disabilities or impairments; 'Learnability', which measures how quickly and efficiently users can learn to use the system; and 'API contract', which specifies the rules and guidelines for how an API should behave. By adhering to these requirements, developers can create systems and applications that are inclusive, efficient, and compliant with relevant laws and regulations.

element.name: Business Agnostic Orchestration Solutions
element.documentation:
Description: Orchestration Solutions ABB is a grouping that refers to actual solutions that facilitate the management, scheduling, and monitoring of complex workflows and data processing pipelines. These solutions are primarily used for orchestrating tasks across different systems and technologies, and for building both batch and streaming data processing pipelines.
Additional information: Orchestration Solutions ABB includes tools like Apache Airflow and Apache Beam. Apache Airflow is an open-source platform used for authoring, scheduling, and monitoring workflows. It allows users to define complex workflows as code, making it easier to manage and orchestrate tasks across different systems and technologies. Apache Beam, on the other hand, is an open-source unified programming model and set of tools for building batch and streaming data processing pipelines. It provides a high-level API that allows developers to write data processing logic once and execute it on various distributed processing backends.
Example: Examples of application for Orchestration Solutions ABB include using Apache Airflow to automate the execution of SQL queries and data transfers, or using Apache Beam to build a data processing pipeline that can handle both real-time and batch data.

element.name: Tax Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NNBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Tax Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NNBI) ABB is a grouping that covers a range of legislative measures, policies, and regulations aimed at promoting and ensuring the interoperability of different tax systems and behaviours. It encompasses the rules and standards that govern how different tax systems interact and communicate with each other, with the goal of facilitating seamless and efficient tax operations.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The NNBI ABB is a crucial component in the global tax landscape, as it helps to ensure that different tax systems can work together effectively. This is particularly important in an increasingly globalized world, where businesses and individuals often operate across multiple tax jurisdictions. The NNBI ABB includes legislation and regulations that dictate how different tax systems should interact, as well as standards and protocols for data exchange and communication. It also covers measures aimed at promoting behavioural interoperability, which refers to the ability of different tax systems to adapt and respond to changes in taxpayer behaviour. This can involve measures such as behavioural nudges, which are designed to encourage compliance with tax laws.
Example: Examples of application of the NNBI ABB could include legislation requiring multinational corporations to report their tax information in a standardized format, to facilitate data exchange between different tax jurisdictions. It could also include regulations that mandate the use of certain communication protocols for tax data exchange, to ensure that different tax systems can communicate effectively. On the behavioural side, it could involve policies that use behavioural insights to design tax systems that are more effective at encouraging compliance.

element.name: Business Agnostic Blockchain Solutions
element.documentation:
Description: Blockchain Solutions ABB is a grouping that refers to actual solutions that facilitate the use of blockchain technology in various industries. These solutions are designed to leverage the unique features of blockchain such as decentralization, transparency, security, and immutability to improve business processes, enhance trust, and reduce operational costs.
Additional information: Blockchain Solutions ABB encompasses a wide range of services and applications that utilize blockchain technology. These solutions can be tailored to meet the specific needs of different industries, including finance, supply chain, healthcare, and more. They can be used to create secure and transparent transaction networks, track and verify the authenticity of goods, manage digital identities, and much more. Blockchain Solutions ABB can also include consulting services to help businesses understand and implement blockchain technology effectively.
Example: Examples of Blockchain Solutions ABB include blockchain-based supply chain management systems that provide end-to-end visibility and traceability of goods, blockchain-based financial systems that enable secure and transparent transactions, and blockchain-based healthcare systems that ensure the security and privacy of patient data. Another example is the use of blockchain for energy trading, where ABB has developed a solution that allows for peer-to-peer energy transactions, improving efficiency and reducing costs.

element.name: European Non-Binding Instruments
element.documentation:
Definition: European Non-Binding Instruments (ENBI) is a grouping that covers a range of legislative documents and recommendations that aim to guide and influence the development and implementation of interoperability in various sectors across Europe. These instruments, while not legally binding, provide a framework for cooperation and coordination among European institutions, member states, and other stakeholders.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The ENBI catalogue is divided into three main categories: Governance, Structural, and Behavioural Interoperability. The Governance Interoperability category includes instruments such as the Commission Recommendation 87/598/EEC and Regulation (EU) 2021/694. The Structural Interoperability category includes instruments like the European Interoperability Framework - Implementation Strategy COM/2017/0134 final and the Strengthened Code of Practice on Disinformation. The Behavioural Interoperability category, while currently empty, is intended to house future instruments related to the behavioural aspects of interoperability. These instruments provide guidance on a wide range of issues, from electronic payments and digital programs to disinformation and digital identity frameworks.
Example: Commission Recommendation 87/598/EEC of 8 December 1987 This recommendation provides a code of conduct for electronic payments, outlining the relationships between financial institutions, traders, service establishments, and consumers.
Regulation (EU) 2021/694 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 29 April 2021 This regulation establishes the Digital Europe Programme and repeals Decision (EU) 2015/2240. It is relevant to the European Economic Area.
European Interoperability Framework - Implementation Strategy COM/2017/0134 final This communication from the Commission outlines the implementation strategy for the European Interoperability Framework.
Strengthened Code of Practice on Disinformation This 2022 code of practice provides strengthened guidelines for tackling disinformation.
LOST view: LV-Architecture Principles

element.name: Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions (BADS) is a grouping that covers a range of solutions designed to facilitate the mapping of data from various heterogeneous data structures and serializations to the RDF data model. These solutions are not specific to any particular business or industry, making them versatile and adaptable across different contexts. The key element in this grouping is the RDF Mapping Language (RML), a generic mapping language that extends the W3C-standardized mapping language, R2RML.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions catalogue primarily includes the RDF Mapping Language (RML), a mapping language that allows for the expression of customized mapping rules from various data structures and serializations to the RDF data model. RML is a superset of R2RML, the W3C standard for expressing customized mappings from relational databases to RDF. As such, RML follows the same syntax as R2RML and extends its applicability and scope by adding support for data in other structured formats. RML mappings are themselves RDF graphs, and this document provides a comprehensive description of the RML language and its concepts through definitions and examples.
Example: An example of the application of Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions would be in a scenario where a business needs to map data from a relational database to RDF. Using RML, the business can express customized mapping rules to convert the data from the relational database into the RDF data model. This allows for greater interoperability and flexibility in data management and usage.

element.name: Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI) is a grouping that covers a range of directives and regulations enacted by the European Parliament and Council. These legislative instruments aim to harmonize and modernize various sectors including electronic communications, digital content and services, public procurement, insurance distribution, payment services, cross-border parcel delivery services, cross-border payments, geo-blocking, and electronic commerce within the European Union (EU). The purpose of these legislations is to promote transparency, competition, innovation, consumer protection, and fair trade practices across the EU's internal market.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The EBI catalogue includes various directives and regulations that govern different sectors within the EU. These legislative instruments have been enacted with the aim of harmonizing rules and regulations across member states, promoting competition and innovation, protecting consumer rights, and ensuring fair trade practices. They cover a wide range of areas including electronic communications, digital content and services, public procurement, insurance distribution, payment services, cross-border parcel delivery services, cross-border payments, geo-blocking, and electronic commerce. Each legislation has specific objectives and requirements that must be adhered to by the relevant stakeholders.
Example: For instance, Directive (EU) 2018/1972, also known as the European Electronic Communications Code, modernizes and harmonizes the regulatory framework for electronic communications across the EU. On the other hand, Directive (EU) 2019/770 focuses on contracts for the provision of digital content and digital services, aiming to strengthen consumer rights in the digital market. Similarly, Regulation (EU) 2018/302, known as the Geo-blocking Regulation, addresses unjustified geo-blocking and other forms of discrimination based on customers' nationality or location within the internal market.

element.name: Public Policy Officer Concerns
element.documentation:
Definition: Public Policy Officer Concerns ABB is a Grouping that covers the legal aspects and perspectives that a public policy officer needs to consider when interpreting an eGovERA model. This includes understanding the legal implications of policy decisions, the legal framework surrounding the policy area, and how these legal factors interact with other elements of the policy process.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Public Policy Officer Concerns ABB grouping is crucial for public policy officers as it provides a structured approach to understanding and interpreting the legal aspects of an eGovERA model. This includes not only understanding the legal implications of policy decisions, but also how these legal factors interact with other elements of the policy process. This grouping is particularly important for public policy officers who are tasked with designing and implementing policies within a specific legal framework, as it provides them with the tools and knowledge necessary to navigate this complex landscape.
Example: For instance, a public policy officer working on data privacy policies would use the 'Legal view' element of the Public Policy Officer Concerns ABB to understand the legal framework surrounding data privacy, the legal implications of different policy decisions, and how these legal factors interact with other elements of the policy process such as technological capabilities or public opinion.

element.name: Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NBI) is a grouping that covers a set of laws, regulations, and guidelines aimed at ensuring the seamless interaction of different systems, applications, and services. It focuses on the behavior of systems when they interact, ensuring that they operate together effectively and efficiently. The NBI legislation is designed to facilitate the exchange of information and services among different systems, promoting interoperability and integration.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NBI) is an important aspect of information technology and telecommunications. It is concerned with the ability of different systems, applications, and services to work together seamlessly. This involves not only the technical aspects of interoperability but also the legal and regulatory aspects. The NBI legislation provides a framework for ensuring that systems behave in a predictable and consistent manner when they interact, facilitating the exchange of information and services. It covers a wide range of areas, including data exchange standards, communication protocols, interface specifications, and service level agreements.
Example: An example of the application of the Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NBI) is in the healthcare sector. Here, different systems such as electronic health records, hospital information systems, and telemedicine applications need to interact seamlessly to provide effective and efficient healthcare services. The NBI legislation ensures that these systems can exchange information and services in a predictable and consistent manner, promoting interoperability and integration.

element.name: Tax Digital Public Service Consumers Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Tax Digital Public Service Consumers Catalogue ABB is a Grouping that covers a range of business actors involved in the administration, regulation, and interaction with tax-related digital public services. These actors include social security administration, businesses, citizens, customs authorities, statistical authorities, quality control authorities, public administration, tributary justice courts, tax ombudsmen, temporary excise taxpayers, registered excise tax payers, and tax administration.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Tax Digital Public Service Consumers Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive list of all the business actors that interact with tax-related digital public services. These actors play various roles in the tax system, from administration and regulation to compliance and dispute resolution. The catalogue is designed to provide a clear understanding of the different roles and responsibilities in the tax system, and to facilitate the development and implementation of digital public services in the tax sector.
Example: For instance, the 'Social Security Administration' is a business actor responsible for administering social security programs, while the 'Business' actor represents businesses that interact with digital public services for tax purposes. 'Citizen' represents individual taxpayers who use digital public services for their tax affairs. 'Customs Authority' and 'Statistical Authorities' are involved in the regulation and monitoring of tax-related activities. 'Quality Control Authority' ensures the standards and compliance in tax-related activities. 'Public Administration' and 'Tax Administration' are overarching actors responsible for the overall administration and regulation of the tax system. 'Tributary Justice Court' and 'Tax Ombudsman' are involved in resolving tax-related disputes. 'Temporary Excise Taxpayers' and 'Registered Excise Tax Payer' represent different types of taxpayers in the excise tax system.
LOST view: OV-Digital Public Service Consumers

'Quality Control Authority' ensures the standards and compliance in tax-related activities. 'Public Administration' and 'Tax Administration' are overarching actors responsible for the overall administration and regulation of the tax system. 'Tributary Justice Court' and 'Tax Ombudsman' are involved in resolving tax-related disputes. 'Temporary Excise Taxpayers' and 'Registered Excise Tax Payer' represent different types of taxpayers in the excise tax system.

Definition: Test Enablers ABB is a Grouping that refers to the applications and services that support the development and deployment of conformance testing and validation.

Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): Interoperability Testbed - The Test Bed allows users to execute predefined test cases on their systems in order to test the conformance to standards and requirements, simulate a web-service, validate content and test a complete message exchange protocol. The Testbed manages test cases and users, and orchestrates domain-specific components, the domain-specific logic is in separate components that are used via web services. Test results are provided in a standardised, machine-readable format. The Test Bed also offers a test registry and repository (TRR) to store test artefacts (assertions, test cases, validation schemas, etc.) and compile test services (validation services, simulator services, etc.). element.name: Tax Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (ENBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Tax Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (ENBI) ABB is a grouping that covers the legal and regulatory aspects of tax laws and their impact on the interoperability of different systems and behaviours. It includes the study of how tax laws influence the interaction between different systems, entities or processes and how they can be designed or modified to promote better interoperability.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The ENBI ABB is an essential tool for policymakers, tax professionals, and IT specialists. It helps in understanding the complex interplay between tax legislation and behavioural interoperability. This includes how tax laws can affect the way different systems interact, how data is shared and processed, and how different entities cooperate to achieve common goals. The ENBI ABB also explores how tax laws can be designed or modified to promote better interoperability, efficiency, and compliance. This can involve changes to the tax code, the introduction of new technologies, or the development of new procedures and protocols.
Example: For instance, a country might modify its tax laws to encourage the use of a particular type of software or technology. This could make it easier for different systems to interact and share data, leading to greater efficiency and compliance. Alternatively, a country might introduce new tax laws that require certain types of data to be shared or processed in a particular way. This could promote interoperability by ensuring that all systems are using the same standards and protocols.
LOST view: LV-Binding Power and Jurisdiction

element.name: Business Agnostic Digital Business Capabilities Map
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic Digital Business Capabilities Catalogue ABB is a Grouping that refers to the actual catalogue of digital business capabilities (DBC) that puts together a range of capabilities related to various digital business operations. These capabilities are crucial for organizations to effectively and efficiently manage their digital operations, gain valuable insights, make informed decisions, ensure data quality, security, and compliance, and generate value and revenue.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The catalogue includes a wide range of capabilities such as Electronic Identification, Qualification Management, Digital Payments, Digital Procurement, Digital Communication, Digital Exchange, Digital Invoicing, Data Management, Multimedia Management, Contact Management, Case and Workflow Management, Knowledge Management, Digital Twin, Artificial Intelligence, and Business Agnostic Data Management Digital Business Capability Catalogue. Each of these capabilities has a specific role and function in the digital business operations of an organization. For instance, Electronic Identification ensures secure access to online services, Digital Payments enables the purchase of goods or services via digital modes, and Data Management is responsible for the development, execution, and supervision of plans, policies, programs, and practices that deliver, control, protect, and enhance the value of data and information assets throughout their lifecycles.
Example: An example of the application of these capabilities can be seen in a digital business operation where Electronic Identification is used to ensure secure access to online services, Digital Payments are used to facilitate the purchase of goods or services, Digital Communication is used for virtual collaboration, and Data Management is used to manage and enhance the value of data and information assets. Similarly, in the Business Agnostic Data Management Digital Business Capability Catalogue, capabilities such as Data Discovery, Data Analytics, Data Monetization, Data Governance, Data Ethics, Data Interoperability, Data Sharing, Data Quality, Data Security, and Data Lineage are used to effectively and efficiently manage data assets, gain valuable insights, make informed decisions, ensure data quality, security, and compliance, and generate value and revenue.
LOST view: OV-Data Spaces

element.name: Business Agnostic Business Information Base
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic Business Information Base (ABB) is a grouping that refers to the actual catalogue of information entities that covers a wide range of business-related elements. These elements include payments, transactions, identification, qualifications, audit trails, access rights, profiles, messages, availability, digital signatures, documents, security measures, locations, invoices, contracting authorities, economic operators, digital assets, credentials, data quality, and distribution lists.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Business Agnostic Business Information Base (ABB) is a comprehensive catalogue of information entities that are applicable across various business domains. It includes elements such as 'Payment' which refers to the voluntary tendering of money or its equivalent, 'Transaction' which is an interaction of individuals/entities with outside entities, 'Identification' which is data that could potentially be used to identify a particular person or entity, and 'Qualification' which is something that could potentially be used to qualify a particular person or entity. Other elements like 'Audit trail', 'Access rights', 'Profile', 'Message', 'Availability', 'Digital Signature', 'Document', 'Security Measure', 'Location', 'Invoice', 'Contracting authority', 'Economic operator', 'Digital Asset', 'Credential', 'Data Quality', and 'Distribution list' are also part of this catalogue, each with its own specific definition and purpose.
Example: For instance, in a financial institution, the 'Payment' element would refer to the transactions made by customers, 'Identification' would refer to the customer's personal information, 'Access rights' would determine what information a customer or employee can view, 'Digital Signature' would be used to verify the authenticity of digital messages or documents, and 'Data Quality' would refer to the state of qualitative or quantitative pieces of information within the institution.
LOST view: OV-Functional Architecture Principles

element.name: Tax Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Tax Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI) is a grouping that covers a range of European Union directives, regulations, and legal acts related to tax legislation. These elements aim to ensure the interoperability of tax governance across EU member states, covering areas such as value-added tax, excise duty, mutual assistance for tax recovery, tax avoidance prevention, and administrative cooperation in the field of taxation.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The elements within the Tax Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI) catalogue cover a wide range of tax-related legislation and regulations. These include directives and regulations on the common system of taxation, indirect taxes on capital raising, general arrangements for excise duty, and the holding and movement of products subject to excise duty. The catalogue also includes legal acts on refunds to non-EEC taxable persons, the prevention of tax avoidance by companies, and the harmonised structures of excise duties on alcohol and alcoholic drinks. Furthermore, it covers directives encouraging mutual assistance between EU countries for tax recovery, the EU tax dispute resolution system, and cooperation between EU countries' tax administrations.
Example: An example of an element within the Tax Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI) catalogue is the 'Directive 2014/86/EU of the Council of 8 July 2014', which pertains to the common system of taxation applicable in the case of parent companies and subsidiaries of different Member States. Another example is the 'Directive 2006/112/EC of 28 November 2006', which relates to the common system of value added tax.
LOST view: LV-Binding Power and Jurisdiction

element.name: Shared Legal Content
element.documentation:
Definition: Shared Legal Content ABB is a Grouping setting legal (re)usable resources with convergence power, to public policy goals attainment, enabling to reuse and share legislations cross-legal jurisdictions through exchange of data, information, and knowledge.
Source: EUR-LEX
Source reference: (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32021R0695&qid=1646736486403)
Last modification: 2023-11-20

Synonym: ABC
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): The past years have seen an extraordinary proliferation of sharing economy platforms, and the largest platforms have fast become global enterprises with market capitalisations that exceed competitors with “traditional” business concepts. These developments call into question a number of regulatory matters and pose new questions for national and European-level regulators. (https://www.intereconomics.eu/contents/year/2017/number/1/article/regulating-the-european-sharing-economy-state-of-play-and-challenges.html).

Additional information: The degree of achievement could range from an ideal perfect shared legal framework (i.e. no interoperability barriers from the legal perspective) to an imperfect or even null shared legal framework (i.e. some interoperability barriers from the legal perspective). The level of legal interoperability will constrain digital public services cross-legal jurisdictions.

element.name: Digital Solution Non-Functional Requirements Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Interoperability Non-Functional Requirements Catalogue ABB is a Grouping of technical specifications and capabilities that enable different systems, applications, or devices to exchange information and work together seamlessly
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Digital Solution Non-Functional Requirements Catalogue ABB includes various elements such as Extensibility, Observability, Security, Agility, Resiliency, Consistency, Scalability, Availability, Usability, and Durability. Each of these elements has a specific role and importance in the overall system design and operation. For instance, Extensibility refers to the system's ability to accommodate future changes or additions seamlessly, while Observability refers to the system's ability to monitor and analyze its behavior in real-time. Similarly, Security refers to the system's ability to protect itself against unauthorized access and data breaches, while Agility refers to the system's ability to adapt quickly to changing business needs or market conditions. The catalogue also includes various sub-elements under each main element, providing a comprehensive list of non-functional requirements for digital solutions.
Example: An example of applying the Digital Solution Non-Functional Requirements Catalogue ABB could be during the design and development of a new digital banking application. The developers would need to consider various non-functional requirements such as Security (to protect users' financial information), Availability (to ensure the app is always accessible), Usability (to ensure the app is user-friendly), Scalability (to handle increasing number of users), and Extensibility (to easily add new features in the future). Additionally, they would also need to consider sub-elements such as Confidentiality and Integrity under Security, Accessibility and Learnability under Usability, and Disaster Recovery and Recoverability under Resiliency.

The catalogue includes elements such as the Anonymisation Policy, which outlines the rules and procedures for anonymizing sensitive data in compliance with privacy regulations.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Privacy Data Policy Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of policies and guidelines that an organization uses to safeguard personal data. It includes elements like the Anonymisation Policy, which is a formal document outlining the methods, techniques, and criteria used to transform personally identifiable information (PII) into a form that can no longer be linked to an individual. This policy ensures compliance with privacy regulations and helps mitigate the risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of personal data. It includes considerations for data anonymization processes, such as data masking, aggregation, or encryption, to protect individuals' privacy while still allowing data to be used for legitimate business purposes.
Example: An example of an element in the Privacy Data Policy Catalogue ABB is the Anonymisation Policy. This policy could state that all customer data used for internal analytics must first be anonymized through a process of data masking. This would involve replacing identifiable data fields with artificial identifiers or pseudonyms to prevent the identification of individuals. The policy might also specify the use of encryption for data storage and transmission to further protect personal data from unauthorized access or disclosure.

element.name: Business Agnostic Data Space Participant Digital Public Service Catalog
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic Data Space Participant Digital Public Service Catalog (ABB) is a grouping that covers a range of digital public services that are essential for the operation and management of data in a business-agnostic manner. These services include data extraction, transformation and loading, content management, open data management, workflow management, data exchange, eArchiving, anonymisation, and secure access control.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Business Agnostic Data Space Participant Digital Public Service Catalog ABB is a comprehensive catalog that encompasses various digital public services that are not specific to any business or industry. These services are crucial for the efficient handling and management of data. 'Data Extraction, Transformation and Loading' refers to the process of extracting data from different sources, transforming it into a usable format, and loading it into a database. 'Content Management' involves the creation, management, and modification of digital content. 'Open Data Management' is about managing data that is freely available to everyone to use and republish. 'Workflow Management' is the coordination of tasks that make up a work process. 'Data Exchange' is the process of transferring data from one system to another. 'eArchiving' is the storage of digital data for long-term preservation. 'Anonymisation' is the process of removing personally identifiable information from data sets. 'Secure Access Control' is about managing access to resources in a computing environment.
Example: Examples of application include a government agency using the 'Open Data Management' service to manage and share public data, a healthcare organization using 'Anonymisation' service to protect patient data, or a corporation using 'Workflow Management' to streamline its business processes.

element.name: Agility Requirements Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Agility Requirements Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a set of IT non-functional requirements that contribute to the agility of a software or system. These requirements, including configurability, compatibility, maintainability, and deployability, are crucial for ensuring that the system can adapt to changing needs and environments, can function seamlessly with other systems, can be easily modified and maintained, and can be efficiently deployed and installed.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Agility Requirements Catalogue ABB comprises of four key elements: Configurability, Compatibility, Maintainability, and Deployability. Configurability refers to the system's ability to be easily customized or modified to meet specific needs, without requiring extensive programming knowledge. Compatibility ensures that the system can function properly with other systems, hardware, or environments, and can be easily upgraded or migrated. Maintainability refers to the ease with which the system can be modified, updated, or repaired, contributing to its long-term sustainability. Deployability involves the ease and efficiency with which the software can be deployed and installed on different platforms, reducing downtime and minimizing risk of errors.
Example: An example of the application of the Agility Requirements Catalogue ABB could be in the development of a new software system. The developers would need to ensure that the system is configurable, allowing users to easily customize it to their needs. They would also need to ensure that it is compatible with a range of other systems, software, and hardware to ensure wide usability. The system should be maintainable, with clear documentation and a modular design to allow for easy updates and repairs. Finally, the system should be easily deployable, with a straightforward installation process that minimizes disruption to the existing system.

element.name: Digital Public Service Improvement Principle Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Digital Public Service Improvement Principle Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers the principles, guidelines, and strategies aimed at enhancing the delivery of public services through digital platforms. The catalogue primarily focuses on the principle of 'Innovation', which is a key driver in the modernization and improvement of public services.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Digital Public Service Improvement Principle Catalogue ABB is an essential tool for public service organizations seeking to leverage digital technologies to improve their service delivery. The catalogue's main element is 'Innovation', which refers to the application of new ideas, methods, or technologies to enhance public service delivery. Innovation in this context can involve the development of new digital services, the improvement of existing services through digital technologies, or the use of digital technologies to create new ways of engaging with the public. The catalogue provides a framework for understanding and applying the principle of innovation in the context of digital public service improvement.
Example: An example of the application of the Digital Public Service Improvement Principle Catalogue ABB could be a local government agency using it as a guide to develop a new online service for residents to report issues in their community. The agency could use the principle of 'Innovation' to explore new ways of receiving and responding to reports, such as through a mobile app or a chatbot, thereby improving the efficiency and accessibility of their service.

element.name: Secure Public Network Solutions
element.documentation:
Definition: Secure Public Network Solutions ABB is a Grouping that covers a range of network solutions designed to ensure secure and reliable communication in public networks. These solutions include the Common Communication Network (CCN) and Common Communication Network 2 (CCN 2), both of which are designed to facilitate secure and efficient communication across public networks.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Secure Public Network Solutions ABB is a comprehensive catalogue of network solutions that are designed to enhance the security and reliability of communication in public networks. The catalogue includes the Common Communication Network (CCN) and Common Communication Network 2 (CCN 2). The CCN is a communication network that is commonly used for secure and reliable communication in public networks. Similarly, the CCN 2 is an upgraded version of the CCN that offers enhanced features and capabilities for secure and efficient communication in public networks. Both these solutions are designed with advanced security features to protect against potential threats and vulnerabilities in public networks.
Example: Examples of application of the Secure Public Network Solutions ABB include public institutions like government agencies and organizations that require secure and reliable communication networks. These solutions can also be used in industries such as telecommunications, finance, and healthcare where secure and efficient communication is critical.

element.name: Tax Business Information Base
element.documentation:
Definition: Tax Business Information Base ABB is a Grouping that covers a wide range of elements related to tax and business information. This includes information on taxes due on various assets, dispute information, fiscal studies, customs union information, banking data, tax and excise information, declaration of excise, income/transfer, exports information, coding system information, and many more. The purpose of these elements is to provide comprehensive data and information related to taxation and business.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Tax Business Information Base ABB is a comprehensive collection of elements that provide detailed information on various aspects of taxation and business. This includes, but is not limited to, information on taxes due on loans, mortgages, tangible and intangible assets, information on disputes, fiscal studies, customs union, shares/stock options, banking data, tax and excise, income/transfer, exports, coding system, carbon/non-carbon emissions, autonomous tariff suspensions and quota, right to privacy, fiscal calendar, decisions and rulings, transactions, confiscated assets, tax payments, imports, business sector reference, audit information, VAT, prepared statements (ECJ), basic taxpayer information, VAT returns, tax payer behavior/history, comparison data, and tax statements.
Example: For instance, the 'Taxes due on loans and mortgages' element provides information on the taxes that are due on loans and mortgages. The 'Dispute information' element provides data on any disputes related to taxation. The 'Fiscal studies' element provides information on studies conducted on fiscal matters. The 'Non preferential origin good information' element provides data on goods that do not have a preferential origin. Similarly, each element in the Tax Business Information Base ABB provides specific information related to taxation and business.

element.name: Digital Public Service Operation Principle Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Digital Public Service Operation Principle Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a range of principles and guidelines that are essential for the operation of digital public services. These principles include convergence control on public policy goals attainment, data accessibility, data findability, data interoperability, data reusability, preservation of information, security by design, and trust.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Digital Public Service Operation Principle Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of principles that guide the operation of digital public services. 'Convergence control on public policy goals attainment' refers to the alignment of digital services with public policy goals. 'Data Accessibility' and 'Data Findability' pertain to the ease of access and discovery of data respectively. 'Data Interoperability' and 'Data Reusability' concern the ability of systems to work together and the potential for data to be reused. 'Preservation of information' is about maintaining and protecting data, while 'Security by Design' is a principle that emphasizes the importance of incorporating security measures from the onset of system design. Lastly, 'Trust' refers to the confidence and reliability in digital public services.
Example: An example of the application of these principles can be seen in a digital public service like an online tax filing system. The system should be designed with 'Security by Design', ensuring that user data is protected. The data collected should be 'Accessible' and 'Findable' for users, and 'Interoperable' to allow for seamless interaction with other systems. The system should also allow for 'Data Reusability', enabling data to be used for multiple purposes. The 'Preservation of Information' is crucial to maintain historical tax records. The system should also align with the 'Convergence control on public policy goals attainment' by facilitating the efficient collection of taxes. Lastly, the system should foster 'Trust' among users by being reliable and secure.

element.name: National Binding Instruments
element.documentation:
Definition: National Binding Instruments (NBI) is a grouping that covers a broad range of legislative and regulatory frameworks related to interoperability in various domains. This includes structural, behavioural, and governance interoperability. The NBI provides a structured approach to the implementation and management of these frameworks, ensuring that they are in line with national and international standards and best practices.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The National Binding Instruments (NBI) catalogue is a comprehensive repository of legislative and regulatory frameworks that govern interoperability in various domains. It includes the Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI), which covers the National Schema on eIdentification, Cybersecurity, eDelivery, and access to Base Registries. It also includes the Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NBI) and the Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NBI). Each of these categories contains specific elements that provide detailed information on the respective legislative and regulatory frameworks. The NBI catalogue is designed to facilitate the implementation and management of these frameworks, ensuring compliance with national and international standards and best practices.
Example: For instance, under the Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI), there are specific elements such as the National Schema on eIdentification which provides guidelines on electronic identification processes. Similarly, the National Schema on Cybersecurity outlines the legislative framework for managing cybersecurity risks. The National Schema on eDelivery provides the regulatory framework for electronic delivery services, while the National Schema on the access to Base Registries outlines the guidelines for accessing base registries. These elements provide a structured approach to implementing and managing interoperability in their respective domains.
