NARRATIVE: The TVA-Digital Workplace Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements of the Business Agnostic Digital Workplace Business Services and Digital Workplace Enablers.
The Business Agnostic Digital Workplace Business Services is a Diagram Model-group ABB. It is designed to be universally applicable across various business domains. Within this model group, there is a Business Service ABB named Digital Collaboration. This service is described as a Digital Collaboration Digital Public Service, indicating its role in facilitating digital interaction and cooperation in the public sector.
On the other hand, the Digital Workplace Enablers is a Grouping ABB. This grouping refers to components or services that enable the collaboration of work aspects while ensuring security and privacy. Within this grouping, there is an Application Service ABB also named Digital Collaboration. This service, while sharing the same name as the one in the Business Agnostic Digital Workplace Business Services, is distinct in its function and application.
The relationship between these elements is that they are all part of the overarching TVA-Digital Workplace Enablers [Motivation] view. They are interconnected in their shared goal of enabling digital collaboration in the workplace, albeit through different means and in different contexts. The motivation behind these elements and their relationships is to create a comprehensive framework that leverages digital technologies to enhance collaboration and productivity in the workplace, while also ensuring the security and privacy of all involved.

node.label: Business Agnostic Digital Workplace Business Services

view.name: TVA-Data Space Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Data Space Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various components and services that support the creation and management of a dataspace. This view is divided into three main elements: Dataspace Enablers, Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue, and Business Agnostic Dataspace Solutions.
The Dataspace Enablers, a Grouping ABB, refers to components and services that support the creation and management of a dataspace. Within this grouping, there are two Application Service ABBs: Dataspace and Dataspace Connector. The Dataspace is the virtual space that enables the creation of a single market for data by integrating, transforming, and making available such data. The Dataspace Connector enables the easy and trustworthy procedure to share data and work collaboratively with other research institutions.
The Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue is another Grouping ABB that includes two Business Service ABBs: Data Space and Data Space Participant. These services are part of the digital public service offerings related to the dataspace.
The third element, Business Agnostic Dataspace Solutions, is a Grouping ABB that includes several Application Service SBBs. These are specific solutions for the dataspace, including the Eclipse Dataspace Connector, International Data Space Connector, FIWARE TRUE Connector, Sovity Dataspace Connector, Intel IONOS Orbiter Connector, and Fraunhofer AISEC Trusted Connector. Each of these services provides specific functionalities and capabilities within the dataspace.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive overview of the various components, services, and solutions that enable the creation, management, and utilization of a dataspace. This view helps in understanding the technical and business aspects of the dataspace and how they interact with each other. It also helps in identifying potential opportunities for improvement and innovation within the dataspace.

view.name: TVA-Artificial Intelligence Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Artificial Intelligence Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) in a business context. This view is composed of two main elements: "Business Agnostic Artificial Intelligence Business Service" and "Artificial Intelligence Enablers".
The "Business Agnostic Artificial Intelligence Business Service" is a Diagram Model-group ABB that represents a business service that is independent of any specific business context. It contains a single element, "Business Intelligence", which is a Business Service ABB that provides a digital public service related to business intelligence.
The "Artificial Intelligence Enablers" is a Grouping ABB that refers to components and services that provide the necessary infrastructure and resources for AI developers to build intelligent systems. These systems are capable of performing tasks that typically require human-like intelligence, such as perception, reasoning, learning, and decision-making. This grouping contains four elements: "Artificial Intelligence", "Machine Learning", "Artificial Intelligence Engine", and "Natural-Language Processing (NLP)".
"Artificial Intelligence" is an Application Service ABB that enables procedures to display intelligent behaviour by analysing their environment and taking actions with some degree of autonomy to achieve specific objectives.
"Machine Learning" is an Application Service ABB within the field of AI that enables systems to automatically learn and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed. It involves the development and deployment of algorithms and models that can analyze large volumes of data, identify patterns, and make predictions or decisions based on the learned patterns.
"Artificial Intelligence Engine" is an Application Service ABB that refers to a software component or service that encompasses the core capabilities of an AI system. It provides a set of algorithms, models, and tools that enable the development, deployment, and execution of AI applications. The AI engine acts as the brain behind AI-powered systems, enabling tasks such as data processing, pattern recognition, prediction, decision-making, and learning.
"Natural-Language Processing (NLP)" is an Application Service ABB that deals with the interaction between computers and humans using natural language. The ultimate objective of NLP is to read, decipher, understand, and make sense of the human language in a valuable way.
In summary, the TVA-Artificial Intelligence Enablers [Motivation] view provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging AI in a business context, including the necessary infrastructure, resources, and services to enable the development and deployment of intelligent systems.

node.label: Business Agnostic Artificial Intelligence Business Service

view.name: TVA-Trust Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Trust Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that facilitate secure cross-border transactions and interactions.
The view includes three main groups: Business Agnostic Trust Business Services, Business Agnostic Blockchain Business Service, and Trust Enablers.
The Business Agnostic Trust Business Services group includes the eSignature service, which is a digital public service that enables the signing of data in electronic form by a natural person.
The Business Agnostic Blockchain Business Service group includes the Digital Immutability service, which is a digital public service that ensures the integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation of digitally signed documents.
The Trust Enablers group refers to components and services that facilitate the establishment and maintenance of secure cross-border transactions and interactions. This group includes various application services such as e-Seal Preservation, e-Timestamp Verification and Validation, Registered Electronic Delivery, e-Seal Verification and Validation, e-Signature Creation, e-Signature Preservation, e-Signature Verification and Validation, e-Seal Creation, e-Timestamp Creation, and Trust Service Provisioning.
These services enable various procedures such as extending the trustworthiness of the qualified electronic signature beyond the technological validity period, verifying timestamps used for establishing evidence that a given piece of data existed at a given point in time, transmitting sensitive or confidential documents and messages between parties, verifying documents that are signed electronically, signing data in electronic form by a natural person, and creating, verifying, or validating electronic signatures, time stamps, seals, electronically registered delivery services, and certificates.
The Trust Enablers group also includes the Blockchain Enablers, which refers to components and services that facilitate the development, deployment, and management of ledger technology applications. This includes the Blockchain and Distributed Ledger application services, which enable secure, transparent, and immutable record-keeping and transaction processing shared by all participants in a network.
The view also includes the Business Agnostic Blockchain Solutions group, which includes the Ethereum and European Blockchain Services Infrastructure application services. These services facilitate the development, deployment, and management of blockchain technology applications.
In addition, the view includes various application services such as Digital Certification Timestamp, Digital Certification eSeal, Digital Certification eSignature Service, Digital Europe eSignature DSS open-source library, and Integrity Verification. These services enable various procedures such as verifying timestamps used for establishing evidence that a given piece of data existed at a given point in time, verifying documents that are signed electronically, securely signing electronic documents using digital certificates, and ensuring that information has not been altered in an unauthorized manner since it was created, transmitted, or stored.

view.name: TVA-Knowledge Discovery Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Knowledge Discovery Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements of the JSON provided. The view is primarily composed of two main elements: the 'Business Agnostic Knowledge Discovery Service' and the 'Knowledge Discovery Enablers'.
The 'Business Agnostic Knowledge Discovery Service' is a Diagram Model-group ABB that encapsulates the 'Knowledge Management' Business Service ABB. This service is described as a digital public service that is dedicated to the management of knowledge. However, the JSON does not provide any sub-elements or further details about this service.
The 'Knowledge Discovery Enablers' is a Grouping ABB that refers to components and services that facilitate the process of discovering insights and knowledge from data. This group includes four Application Service ABBs: 'Knowledge Discovery', 'Knowledge Management', 'Knowledge Exchange', and 'Vocabulary Hub'.
The 'Knowledge Discovery' service is described as a highly complex process where a lot of data manipulation tools with different characteristics have to be used together to reach the goal of previously unknown, potentially useful information extraction.
The 'Knowledge Management' service is a software application or service that supports the processes of capturing, organizing, storing, retrieving, and sharing knowledge within an organization. It provides functionalities and tools to facilitate knowledge creation, acquisition, categorization, search, collaboration, and dissemination. This service enables employees or users to access and leverage the organization's knowledge assets effectively, fostering innovation, decision-making, and continuous learning.
The 'Knowledge Exchange' service is not described in detail in the JSON, but it can be inferred that it is related to the exchange or sharing of knowledge.
The 'Vocabulary Hub' service is also not described in detail in the JSON. However, it can be inferred that it is a service related to managing and providing access to a vocabulary or set of terminologies used within the organization or system.
In summary, the TVA-Knowledge Discovery Enablers [Motivation] view provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various services and components that enable the discovery, management, exchange, and use of knowledge in an organization.

view.name: TVA-Orchestration Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Orchestration Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that facilitate business agnostic orchestration.
The first element is the "Business Agnostic Orchestration Business Service," which is a Diagram Model-group ABB. This element encapsulates the "Workflow Management" service, a Business Service ABB that provides a digital public service for managing workflows.
The second element is the "Orchestration Enablers," a Grouping ABB that refers to the components and practices supporting the development and deployment of orchestration applications. This group includes three sub-elements: "Orchestration" as an Application Service ABB, "Orchestration" as an Application Component ABB, and "Workflow Management" as an Application Service ABB. The "Orchestration" Application Service ABB enables the definition of the sequence and conditions in which one service invokes other services to realize some useful function. The "Orchestration" Application Component ABB enables the coordination and management of the execution of multiple components or services within an application or system. The "Workflow Management" Application Service ABB, also known as Orchestration Application Service, refers to a software solution or service that enables the design, execution, and coordination of workflows within an organization.
The third element is the "Business Agnostic Orchestration Solutions," a Grouping SBB that serves as a catalogue for orchestration solutions. This group includes two sub-elements: "Apache Airflow" and "Apache Beam," both of which are Application Service SBBs. These services represent specific orchestration solutions that can be utilized in the orchestration process.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive understanding of the various elements and their interrelations that enable effective orchestration in a business-agnostic manner. This includes the services, components, and specific solutions that can be leveraged to design, execute, and manage workflows and orchestration processes within an organization.

view.name: TVA-Translation Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Translation Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements related to translation services and solutions. This view is composed of three main elements: 'Business Agnostic eTranslation Services', 'Translation Enablers', and 'Business Agnostic Translation Solutions'.
The 'Business Agnostic eTranslation Services' is a Diagram Model-group ABB that encapsulates the business services related to eTranslation. It includes the 'eTranslation' Business Service ABB, which represents the digital public service for eTranslation. This service is business-agnostic, meaning it can be applied across various business domains.
The 'Translation Enablers' is a Grouping ABB that refers to tools or components that facilitate the translation of text from one language to another using machine learning techniques. It includes the 'Machine Translation' Application Service ABB, which enables the procedures for automated translation of text, metadata, and concept classes or nomenclatures. This application service is a key enabler for the translation process, leveraging machine learning techniques to automate and streamline the translation tasks.
The 'Business Agnostic Translation Solutions' is a Grouping SBB that represents a catalogue of translation solutions. It includes the 'eTranslation' Application Service SBB, which represents the application service for eTranslation. This service is part of the translation solutions that are business-agnostic, meaning they can be applied across various business domains.
In terms of relations, the 'Business Agnostic eTranslation Services' and 'Business Agnostic Translation Solutions' are related as they both provide business-agnostic services and solutions for translation. The 'Translation Enablers' is related to both as it provides the necessary tools and components that enable the translation services and solutions. The motivation behind these elements is to provide comprehensive and versatile translation services and solutions that can be applied across various business domains, leveraging machine learning techniques to automate and streamline the translation tasks.

view.name: TVA-Identification and Access Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Identification and Access Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the secure identification and authentication of users, systems, and services into a platform. This view is composed of three main elements: Identification and Access Enablers, Business Agnostic Identity Management Solutions, and Business Agnostic Authentication Solutions.
The Identification and Access Enablers is a Grouping ABB that refers to components enabling the secure identification and authentication of users, systems, and services into a platform. It includes several Application Service ABBs and Application Component ABBs, such as Authentication, Registration, Identification, Access Management, Identity Management, Authorisation, Accounting, Request Validation, Centralized Identity Management, and Decentralized Identity Management. Each of these components plays a crucial role in the process of identification and access enabling, from the registration of users to the management of their identities and access rights.
The Business Agnostic Identity Management Solutions is a Grouping SBB that includes several Application Service SBBs, such as eIDAS-Node, eIDAS-Proxy-Service, Keycloak, EU Login, WSO2 Identity Server, and Fraunhofer Omejdn Server. These solutions provide a range of identity management services, from the provision of personal identification data to the management of user authentication and authorization.
The Business Agnostic Authentication Solutions is another Grouping SBB that includes several Application Service SBBs, such as EU Login Identification, EU Login Authentication, EU Login Request Validation, and EU Login Registration. These solutions provide a range of authentication services, from user identification to request validation and registration.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework for the secure identification and authentication of users, systems, and services into a platform. This is achieved through a combination of various components and solutions, each playing a specific role in the process. The ultimate goal is to ensure that only authorized users have access to the platform and its services, thereby enhancing the security and integrity of the platform.

view.name: TVA-Governance Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The view connects Architecture principles to technical view and the governance components. It is a relevant aspect of solutions architecture. This view specifically examines how architecture principles influence the design and implementation of governance structures within the application layer of a solution.
Firstly, it establishes effective governance within the application layer. Architecture principles provide guidance on defining governance structures, policies, and processes for application and infrastructure development and management. By aligning governance components with these principles, solutions architects design a robust governance framework that promotes compliance, transparency, and accountability in application development, configuration, and operations. This alignment ensures proper control and management of applications, reducing risks and enhancing overall governance practices.
Secondly, aligning architecture principles with governance components supports optimized application development and deployment. Architecture principles often emphasize best practices for application design, scalability, and performance optimization. By incorporating these principles into the design and implementation of governance components, solutions architects establish mechanisms for enforcing design patterns, scalability approaches, and performance monitoring.

view.name: TVA-Functional Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The view that relates Architecture principles to application layer view functional components is crucial in solutions architecture. This view focuses on how architecture principles influence the design and implementation of functional components within the application layer.
By aligning architecture principles with application layer view functional components, solutions architects ensure consistency, enhance performance and scalability, promote reusability and maintainability, and support regulatory compliance. This alignment leads to the creation of robust and efficient applications within the application layer, enabling seamless integration, optimal user experience, reduced maintenance effort, and adherence to legal and industry standards.
In summary, aligning Architecture principles with application layer view functional components ensures consistency, enhances performance and scalability, promotes reusability and maintainability, and supports regulatory compliance. By following these principles, solutions architects can design robust and efficient applications within the application layer.

view.name: TVA-Dataspace Enablers
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The [TVA-Dataspace Enablers] view extends technical view application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements and their relationships to enable data integration, management, and usage. This view is composed of several Diagram Model-group ABBs, each containing multiple Application Service ABBs, and a Grouping ABB named [Dataspace Enablers].
The [App Store / Extensions / User Workflows] group includes three services: [Data Integration], [Data Integration Plugins Manager], and [Data Extraction, Transformation and Loading]. These services facilitate the process of combining data from multiple sources into a unified view, managing plugins within a data integration system, and extracting, transforming, and loading data into a target data store.
The [Event Driven / NRT] group contains the [Message Broker] service, which acts as an intermediary for asynchronous message-based communication between different applications.
The [Vocabulary Management] group includes the [Vocabulary Hub] service, a centralized repository for managing and providing access to a wide range of vocabularies or terminologies.
The [Trust] group contains the [Privacy] service, which enables functionalities such as storing, securing, anonymising, pseudonymising, rectifying and erasing personal data.
The [Identity Provider] group includes three services: [Centralized Identity Management], [Decentralized Identity Management], and [Identity Management]. These services manage and control user identities and access rights in both centralized and decentralized manners.
The [Monitoring] group contains the [Observability] service, which provides insights into the internal state and behavior of a system by analyzing its external outputs.
The [Dataspace Enablers] group includes the [Dataspace], [Dataspace Connector], [Dataspace Connector Provider], and [Dataspace Connector Consumer] services. These services support the creation and management of a dataspace, a virtual space for integrating, transforming, and making available data.
The [Contract Negotiation] group includes the [Data Contract], [Data Policy], and [Data Governance] services, which manage the availability, usability, integrity, and security of data within an organization.
The [Service Discovery and Registry], [Service Registry], [Data Catalogue Management], [Dataset Catalogue], and [Federated Data Catalogue Management] services enable the implementation of public digital services, organize metadata about data assets, and manage data catalogues.
The [Data Analytics and Quality] group includes the [Data Analytics] and [Data Quality] services, which analyze data and ensure its accuracy, completeness, consistency, and up-to-dateness.
The view also includes several Archimate Diagram-model ABBs that represent the motivation behind various elements, and Diagram Model-connection ABBs that represent the relationships between these elements.

view.name: TV-Technical Agreements
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The [TV-Technical Agreements] view extends technical view application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various types of agreements, contracts, and specifications to ensure interoperability, collaboration, and service quality across different systems and organizations.
The view includes four types of Technical Agreements: Contract ABB, Grouping ABB, and Business Object ABB. The Contract ABB type includes the Technical Agreement, Technical Interoperability Agreement, and Service Level Agreement. These agreements formalize the framework for strategic and technological collaboration, ensure organizations operate under different technical frameworks, and outline the level of service provided and the metrics used to measure service quality, respectively.
The Grouping ABB type includes the API Technical Interoperability Agreement Solutions, BlockChain Technical Interoperability Agreement Catalogue, and Identity and Access Management Technical Interoperability Agreement Solutions. These groupings provide a collection of technical specifications and standards for building and consuming APIs, ensuring interoperability using blockchain technology, and managing identity and access, respectively.
The Business Object ABB type includes the BlockChain Governance, Hybrid Blockchain Governance, Public BlockChain Governance (permissionless), and Private BlockChain Governance (permissioned). These objects provide the framework and mechanisms for effective collaboration and interoperability using blockchain technology.
The elements within these agreements, contracts, and specifications have relationships with each other based on their function and purpose. For example, the API Technical Interoperability Agreement Solutions grouping includes various Contract ABB elements like OpenAPI, RESTful API, GraphQL, gRPC, JSON-RPC, Simple Object Access Protocol, and OData. These elements provide the technical specifications for building and consuming APIs, enabling interoperability between different systems.
Similarly, the BlockChain Technical Interoperability Agreement Catalogue grouping includes the BlockChain IoP Agreement Contract ABB and the BlockChain Governance, Hybrid Blockchain Governance, Public BlockChain Governance (permissionless), and Private BlockChain Governance (permissioned) Business Object ABB elements. These elements provide the framework and mechanisms for ensuring interoperability using blockchain technology.
The motivation behind these elements and their relationships is to provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging technical agreements, contracts, and specifications to ensure interoperability, collaboration, and service quality across different systems and organizations. This framework enables organizations to identify common interests, prioritize policy dialogue, and develop the necessary tools for strategic and technological collaboration.

view.name: OV-Governance Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The Organizational Governance Architecture Principles view focuses on the relationship between the building blocks for governance at the organizational layer and the principles that influence them. This view is crucial in solutions architecture as it ensures that the design and implementation of governance structures within an organization align with the guiding principles and goals of the organization.
Aligning the Organizational Governance Architecture Principles view with the governance building blocks brings several benefits. Firstly, it establishes a strong governance framework that ensures compliance, accountability, and transparency throughout the organization. By defining and adhering to architecture principles, solutions architects can design governance structures that reflect the organization's values, policies, and legal requirements. This alignment promotes consistent decision-making, risk management, and regulatory compliance, ultimately enhancing the organization's overall governance practices.
Secondly, aligning the Organizational Governance Architecture Principles view supports effective communication and collaboration among stakeholders. The architecture principles provide guidelines for structuring roles, responsibilities, and decision-making processes within the governance building blocks. By considering the principles that influence these building blocks, solutions architects can design governance structures that facilitate clear lines of authority, information flow, and decision rights. This alignment fosters better coordination, accountability, and efficiency in governance activities across the organization.

view.name: OV-Functional Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The Organizational-Functional Architecture Principles view is a crucial aspect of solutions architecture, as it directly influences the implementation of solutions within an organization's functional layers. This view focuses on aligning the design and implementation of solutions with the goals, requirements, and processes of the organization.
Aligning the Organizational-Functional Architecture Principles view with the organizational building blocks brings several benefits. Firstly, it ensures consistency and coherence across different functional areas within the organization. By defining and adhering to architecture principles, solutions architects establish a standardized approach that allows for seamless integration and interoperability between various building blocks. This consistency fosters effective communication and collaboration among departments and teams, promoting efficient business processes and operations.
Secondly, aligning the Organizational-Functional Architecture Principles view supports the scalability and adaptability of solutions. The architecture principles provide guidelines for designing modular, flexible, and reusable solutions. By considering the specific requirements and characteristics of each organizational building block, solutions architects can design solutions that can easily accommodate future changes and expansions. This scalability and adaptability enable the organization to respond to evolving business needs, reducing the time and resources required for future modifications.
Furthermore, aligning the Organizational-Functional Architecture Principles view enhances governance and decision-making processes within the organization. The architecture principles serve as a reference for making design decisions, ensuring that solutions align with the strategic objectives and priorities of the organization. By considering the unique characteristics and requirements of each building block, solutions architects can make informed choices that optimize resource utilization and support the overall organizational strategy.

view.name: Organisational view [Motivation]
view.documentation: Narrative: The ‘Organisational view – DBCs, DPS and Information” viewpoint extends the organisational view and encompasses the realization of digital business capabilities through the deployment of digital public services that interact with specific information bases. Digital business capabilities represent the technological functions and capacities required to deliver services in a digital environment. These capabilities are leveraged by digital public services, which are designed and implemented to facilitate the delivery of services to users in a digital format. These digital public services rely on accessing and utilizing specific information bases to retrieve and process relevant data. By integrating digital business capabilities, digital public services, and information access, organizations can effectively harness technology to enhance service delivery, streamline processes, and meet the needs of users in the digital realm.

view.name: OV-Data Spaces [Motivation]
view.documentation: Narrative: The ‘Organisational view – DBCs, DPS and Information” viewpoint extends the organisational view and encompasses the realization of digital business capabilities through the deployment of digital public services that interact with specific information bases. Digital business capabilities represent the technological functions and capacities required to deliver services in a digital environment. These capabilities are leveraged by digital public services, which are designed and implemented to facilitate the delivery of services to users in a digital format. These digital public services rely on accessing and utilizing specific information bases to retrieve and process relevant data. By integrating digital business capabilities, digital public services, and information access, organizations can effectively harness technology to enhance service delivery, streamline processes, and meet the needs of users in the digital realm.

view.name: OV-Organisational Agreements
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Organisational Agreements view extends Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that are crucial for the functioning of an organisation. This view is designed to provide a detailed understanding of the organisational agreements and their associated elements.
The first element is the "Organisational Agreement", which is of the type "Contract ABB". The Organisational Agreement ABB is a Contract that enables any agreement to which the Organisation or any Restricted Subsidiary is a party pursuant. This implies that this contract is a binding agreement that the organisation or its restricted subsidiaries must adhere to.
The second element is the "Business Agnostic Organisational Agreement Catalogue", which is of the type "Grouping ABB". This catalogue is a collection of organisational agreements that are business-agnostic, meaning they are applicable regardless of the specific business context or industry. This catalogue includes a sub-element named "National Governance Models", which is of the type "Contract ABB". The National Governance Models are contracts that define the governance models at a national level.
The third element is the "Business Agnostic Organisational Agreement Solutions", which is also of the type "Grouping ABB". This element represents a collection of solutions that are business-agnostic and pertain to organisational agreements. This includes a sub-element named "Code of Conduct for Energy Efficiency in Data Centres", which is of the type "Contract SBB". This contract outlines the code of conduct for maintaining energy efficiency in data centres.
The relationships between these elements are defined by their hierarchical structure. The Organisational Agreement is a standalone element, while the Business Agnostic Organisational Agreement Catalogue and Business Agnostic Organisational Agreement Solutions are groupings that contain specific contracts. These contracts, namely the National Governance Models and the Code of Conduct for Energy Efficiency in Data Centres, are part of their respective groupings and contribute to the overall organisational agreements framework.
The motivation for this structure is to provide a comprehensive and structured view of the organisational agreements, allowing for a clear understanding of the various contracts and their implications. This helps in ensuring compliance and effective governance within the organisation.

view.name: OV-Information Base
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Information Base view extends Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging business objects and grouping ABBs to support the delivery of digital public services.
The view consists of two main elements: 'Information' and 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base'. 'Information' is a Business Object ABB that describes business facts, assets, or opinions that are exchanged in the context of a digital public service to support its delivery. This information is enacted via interpretation rules (expressed in an ontology) of data and considering knowledge of a given context. Examples include an invoice, a medical prescription, a driving license.
The 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base' is a Grouping ABB that serves as a catalogue for various Business Object ABBs. These include 'Payment', 'Transaction', 'Identification', 'Qualification', 'Audit trail', 'Access rights', 'Profile', 'Message', 'Availability', 'Digital Signature', 'Document', 'Security Measure', 'Location', 'Invoice', 'Contracting authority', 'Economic operator', 'Digital Asset', 'Credential', 'Data Quality', and 'Distribution list'. Each of these represents a specific type of business information that is essential for the functioning of the digital public service.
The view also includes a 'Customs Information Base', which is another Grouping ABB. This base contains specific Business Object ABBs related to customs operations, such as 'Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI)', 'Free circulation requirement information', 'Laboratories information', 'Threads and fraudulent actions Information', 'Duties calculation Information', 'Imports information', 'Combined nomenclature', 'Workforce information', 'Classification of goods Information', 'Temporary storage Information', 'Exports information', 'Special Procedures Information', 'Binding Tariffs Information', 'Guarantee Information', 'Economic Operators Information', 'Customs partners Information', 'Economic value Information', 'Internal logistic Information', and 'Origin of goods Information'.
The relations between these elements are not explicitly defined in the JSON, but it can be inferred that the 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base' and 'Customs Information Base' are subsets of the 'Information' element, as they provide specific types of information needed for the digital public service. The motivation behind this structure is to provide a comprehensive and organized view of all the information elements involved in the service, facilitating their management and utilization.

view.name: OV-Digital Public Service Consumers
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Digital Public Service Consumers view extends Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the digital public service delivery model. This model, known as the Digital Public Service Delivery Model ABB, is a Business Collaboration that represents a collection of concepts related to how the public sector delivers digital technologies to citizens and businesses.
Within this model, there are two key business roles: the Digital Public Service Consumer ABB and the Data Consumer ABB. The Digital Public Service Consumer ABB represents the entities that can access and consume public services provided by a public authority. On the other hand, the Data Consumer ABB is responsible for using data provided by other roles or systems, either by consuming, analyzing, interpreting, or presenting data. Data consumers may also be accountable for the appropriate and ethical use of the data they consume.
The model also includes a Tax Digital Public Service Consumers Catalogue, which is a Grouping ABB. This catalogue comprises various Business Actor ABBs, including the Social Security Administration, Business, Citizen, Customs authority, Statistical authorities, Quality control authority, Public Administration, Tributary justice court, Tax Ombudsman, Temporary excise taxpayers, Registered excise tax payer, and Tax administration. Each of these actors plays a specific role in the digital public service delivery model.
The relationships between these elements are crucial for the functioning of the model. The Digital Public Service Consumer ABB and the Data Consumer ABB interact with the various Business Actor ABBs in the Tax Digital Public Service Consumers Catalogue to facilitate the delivery of digital public services. The motivation behind these relationships is to ensure that digital public services are delivered efficiently and effectively to the relevant consumers.

view.name: OV-Data Spaces
view.documentation:
The Organisational view models the most salient Architecture Building Blocks and Solution Building blocks that shall be considered in order to support organisational interoperability among providers and users of a public service.
Narrative: The delivery of public services involves various organizations playing different roles within the ecosystem. Public service providers, acting as suppliers, offer public services to citizens, businesses, and public administrations, who act as consumers of these services. The specific public services are documented in public service catalogues, which serve as a reference for service portfolio management. Public service providers can delegate the delivery of these services to public service delivery agents who act on their behalf. To ensure effective service delivery, public service providers can enter into interoperability agreements that define the agreed-upon approach to delivering public services to users.
The delivery of public services relies on the utilization of business capabilities and the exchange of business information. Business capabilities represent the operational functions required to deliver the services, while the exchange of business information facilitates the transfer of relevant data between the involved parties. The exchanged business information is specific to each instance and is governed by business rules derived from organizational interoperability enablers such as organizational structures, procedures, policies, and skills.
Interoperability governance is overseen by the interoperability organizational authority, responsible for establishing and enforcing governance practices. This authority influences the interoperability strategy, which in turn implements the interoperability framework. Interoperability skills, a specialized form of organizational skills, enable organizations to excel in interoperability and effectively participate in the ecosystem.
Security also plays a crucial role in the delivery of digital public services. A security framework, which is a specific form of a security policy, addresses the organization's security-related aspects, ensuring the protection of sensitive information and adherence to security standards.
To support the design and implementation of digital public services, additional solution building blocks are extended. These include organizational agreements, a digital governance plan, a digital public service catalogue, information management, and digital business capabilities. These building blocks provide specific functionalities and capabilities to enhance the development and deployment of digital public services, aligning them with the overarching organizational framework.
Overall, the organizational layer of the solution architecture template outlines the roles, agreements, processes, and governance mechanisms necessary for effective delivery of public services. It emphasizes the importance of interoperability, security, and specialized skills, while incorporating additional solution building blocks to enable the design and implementation of digital public services.

view.name: OV-Digital Public Services Catalogue
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Digital Public Services Catalogue view extends Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the digital transformation of public services. The view is composed of two main elements: the "Digital Public Service Catalogue" and the "Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue".
The "Digital Public Service Catalogue" is a Business Object ABB that enables the index of active digital public services, and their descriptions, provided by a public administration. This ABB is a key interoperability enabler for sharing and provisioning, as well as reusing and consuming of front-office public services.
The "Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue" is a Grouping ABB that includes a variety of Business Service ABBs. These services range from ePayment, Audit, eArchiving, eDelivery, eQualification, eTranslation, Data Extraction, Transformation and Loading, Data Analytics, Delegation of Power, Workflow Management, Knowledge Management, eNotification, eIdentification, Digital Collaboration, Waiting list Management, Open Data Management, Anonymisation, eSignature, Secure Access Control, Content Management, Log Management, eInvoicing, eTendering, Contact Management, Forms Management, Data Exchange, Digital Inmutability, Business Intelligence, Compliance Testing, Data Space, to Data Space Participant. Each of these services represents a specific digital public service provided by the public administration.
The view also includes a "Customs Digital Public Services Catalogue", which is another Grouping ABB. This catalogue includes Business Service ABBs that are specific to customs operations, such as Economic Operators Registry management, EU Customs Trader Portal, Analysis Management, (Internal) Customs logistics management, Centralised Clearance for Import, Determination of the economic value of goods declared for importation, Tariff Registry management, Applications and Requests, Compliance verification management, Duties guarantee management, Origin Registry management, Customs Decisions system, Customs organizational structure management, Duties calculation and payment, Partner authorization, Customs declarations, Procedure Automation System, Preservation of cargo control, Intra-EU purchases and sales, Notification of Arrival, Presentation Notification and Temporary Storage, Classification of goods, Procedures registry management, Tariff Suspensions, Computerised Transit, Risk analysis, Laboratories registry management, EU Customs information exchange, Goods flow analysis and simulations, and Economic Operator management and accreditation.
In summary, the OV-Digital Public Services Catalogue view provides a comprehensive framework for understanding and managing the digital transformation of public services, with a particular focus on interoperability and the sharing and reusing of services.

view.name: OV-Digital Business Capabilities Map
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Digital Business Capabilities Catalogue view extends Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging digital capabilities in public administration. This view is composed of two main elements: "Digital Business Capability" and two Grouping ABBs - "Business Agnostic Digital Business Capabilities Map" and "Customs Digital Business Capabilities Map".
The "Digital Business Capability" is a Capability ABB that corresponds to an ability implemented in a system to enable public administrations to perform an administrative function. This capability does not contain any sub-elements.
The "Business Agnostic Digital Business Capabilities Map" is a Grouping ABB that encompasses a set of Capability SBBs. These capabilities include "Electronic Identification", "Qualification Management", "Digital Payments", "Digital Procurement", "Digital Communication", "Digital Exchange", "Digital Invoicing", "Data Management", "Multimedia Management", "Contact Management", "Case and Workflow Management", "Knowledge Management", "Digital Twin", and "Artificial Intelligence". Each of these capabilities represents a specific digital business capability that can be leveraged by public administrations.
The "Customs Digital Business Capabilities Map" is another Grouping ABB that includes a set of Capability SBBs related to customs operations. These capabilities include "Compliance requirements checks", "Customs cooperation", "Import procedure", "Guarantee", "Tariffs registry management", "Preservation of cargo information", "Cooperation between Customs and Postal Operators", "Transit procedure", "Authorised Economic Operator accreditation", "Risk analysis", "Cooperation between Customs laboratories", "Special procedure", "Laboratories management", "MS' Customs organization management", "Export procedure", and "Duties Calculation and payment", and "Expeditions controls". Each of these capabilities represents a specific digital business capability that can be leveraged by customs administrations.
The relationships between these elements are not explicitly defined in the JSON data, but it can be inferred that the Capability SBBs within each Grouping ABB are related in that they contribute to the overall digital business capabilities of public or customs administrations. The motivation for these elements and their relationships is to provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging digital capabilities in public administration, enabling more efficient and effective operations.

view.name: OV-Digital Public Service Providers
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Digital Public Service Providers view extends Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the digital transformation in the public sector. This view is represented by the 'Digital Public Service Delivery Model' which is a Business Collaboration ABB. This model represents a collection of concepts related to the way in which the public sector delivers digital technologies to citizens and businesses.
Within this model, there are two key roles. The first is the 'Digital Public Service Provider', a Business Role ABB that represents the entity that offers or delivers public services using digital channels and technologies. The goal of these providers is to provide efficient and accessible services to citizens and businesses by leveraging the power of digital technology.
The second role is the 'Data Provider', another Business Role ABB. This role is responsible for providing data to other roles or systems, either by producing, collecting, transforming, or delivering data. Data providers may also be accountable for the quality, security, and availability of the data they provide.
In addition, the 'Digital Public Service Delivery Model' includes a 'Tax Digital Public Service Providers Catalogue', a Grouping ABB that encompasses several Business Actor ABBs. These actors include 'Tax administration', 'Financial Service Provider', 'Property management authority', 'Internal Affairs', and 'Central Liason Office'. Each of these actors plays a specific role in the provision of digital public services, contributing to the overall efficiency and effectiveness of public service delivery.
In summary, the OV-Digital Public Service Providers view provides a detailed representation of the roles, responsibilities, and relationships involved in the delivery of digital public services. This view is crucial for understanding how digital technologies can be leveraged to improve public service delivery and enhance the citizen and business experience.

view.name: SV-Dataset [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Dataset [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various types of data objects and their associated metadata. This view is primarily composed of three main elements: the Business Agnostic Dataset Catalogue, the Business Agnostic Business Information Base, and the Data Objects ABBs.
The Business Agnostic Dataset Catalogue is a Grouping ABB that contains several Data Object ABBs, each representing a specific type of metadata. These include Multimedia Object Metadata, Log Metadata, Translation Item Metadata, Transaction Metadata, Exchange Item Metadata, Tender Item Metadata, and Authorised Payment Methods Metadata. Each of these metadata types provides structured information about a specific aspect of data, such as multimedia assets, log events, translation items, transactions, exchange items, tender items, and authorized payment methods. The metadata helps in identifying, organizing, retrieving, analyzing, and managing the corresponding data assets, thereby enabling efficient data operations.
The Business Agnostic Business Information Base is a Diagram Model-group ABB that contains several Business Object ABBs. These represent various types of business information, including Location, Data Quality, Payment, Transaction, Message, Document, Audit Trail, and Availability. Each of these business objects provides specific business-related information, which is crucial for the operation and management of business activities.
The Data Objects ABBs include Dataset, Reference Data, and Master Data. The Dataset ABB represents a collection of related data organized in a structured format. The Reference Data ABB enables the definition of a set of values or codes used to categorize, classify, or describe data elements in a consistent and standardized way. The Master Data ABB enables the implementation of non-transactional information that plays a key role in the core operation of a business in public administrations and is re-used for multiple purposes.
The relationships among these elements are defined by their hierarchical structure in the JSON. The Business Agnostic Dataset Catalogue and the Business Agnostic Business Information Base are at the top level, each containing several sub-elements. The Data Objects ABBs are at the same level as these two main elements, indicating their independent but equally important roles in the data architecture. The motivation behind this structure is to provide a comprehensive and flexible framework for managing a wide range of data types and their associated metadata, thereby supporting efficient data operations and business activities.

view.name: SV-Forms Structure [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Forms Structure [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the Business Agnostic Forms Structure Catalogue and the Business Agnostic Business Information Base.
The Business Agnostic Forms Structure Catalogue is a Grouping ABB that contains several Data Object ABBs, each representing a different type of form. These include the Contact Form, Feedback Form, Survey Form, Registration Form, and Order Form. Each of these forms is a standalone entity with no further elements nested within them.
The Business Agnostic Business Information Base is a Diagram Model-group ABB that contains two Business Object ABBs: Document and Message. The Document represents document information, while the Message represents message information. Similar to the forms in the Business Agnostic Forms Structure Catalogue, these two objects do not contain any further nested elements.
The Forms Structure is a Data Object ABB that enables the implementation of the layout and organization of the fields, labels, and controls on a form used to collect or display data. This structure does not contain any nested elements.
The motivation behind this structure is to provide a clear and organized framework for managing various forms and business information. The Business Agnostic Forms Structure Catalogue groups together different types of forms, making it easier to manage and locate specific forms. The Business Agnostic Business Information Base provides a similar function for business information, grouping together different types of information for easy access and management. The Forms Structure, on the other hand, provides a template for creating and managing the layout of these forms, ensuring consistency and efficiency in data collection and display.

view.name: SV-Data Mapping Catalogue [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Mapping Catalogue [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the business agnostic business information base and the data mapping catalogue.
The first element in this view is the 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base', which is a Diagram Model-group ABB. This base is a general-purpose business information base that is not tied to any specific business context or domain. It contains two sub-elements: 'Availability' and 'Digital Asset', both of which are Business Object ABBs.
'Availability' is a business object that represents the availability information. This could include data about the availability of resources, services, or any other business elements. The 'Digital Asset' business object represents the digital asset information. This could include data about digital resources such as software, digital media, or any other digital assets.
The second main element in this view is the 'Data Mapping Catalogue', which is a Data Object ABB. This catalogue is a data object that aims to index an inventory of rules or procedures on how data from different sources and domains can be linked and integrated. This could include mapping rules, transformation rules, integration procedures, or any other relevant information.
The relationship between these elements is that the 'Data Mapping Catalogue' uses the data from the 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base' to create a comprehensive and integrated view of the business data. This allows for a more effective and efficient use of the data, as it can be easily linked and integrated across different sources and domains.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging business data. By using a business agnostic business information base and a data mapping catalogue, businesses can effectively manage their data and use it to drive business decisions and actions. This can lead to improved business performance and competitiveness.

view.name: SV-High Value Datasets [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-High Value Datasets [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging high-value datasets and business information. This view is composed of several elements, each with unique characteristics and relationships.
The first element, "Business Agnostic High Value Dataset Solutions," is a Grouping ABB that serves as a catalogue for various high-value datasets. These datasets are divided into six Data Object SBBs: "Geospatial High Value Dataset," "Business-related data High Value Dataset," "Metereology High Value Dataset," "Mobility High Value Dataset," "Statistics High Value Dataset," and "Earth Observation Data High Value Dataset." Each of these datasets contains specific data related to their respective fields, such as INSPIRE themes, reference parcels, agricultural parcels, basic company information, records, financial statements, weather data, river information services data, statistical data on select legal acts, and environmental information.
The second element, "Business Agnostic Business Information Base," is a Diagram Model-group ABB that contains three Business Object ABBs: "Availability," "Data Quality," and "Document." These objects provide information on the availability of the datasets, the quality of the data, and any related documents.
The third element, "Dataset," is a Data Object ABB that represents a collection of related data organized and presented in a structured format. This element serves as a foundation for the high-value datasets.
The final element, "High Value Dataset," is a Data Object ABB that represents datasets with the potential to generate significant socio-economic or environmental benefits, innovative services, assist in generating revenues, and be combined with other datasets. This element highlights the value and potential benefits of the datasets.
The relationships between these elements are crucial for understanding the motivation behind the SV-High Value Datasets [Motivation] view. The high-value datasets are grouped under the "Business Agnostic High Value Dataset Solutions" and are supported by the "Business Agnostic Business Information Base," which provides necessary information about the datasets. The "Dataset" and "High Value Dataset" elements further emphasize the importance and value of these datasets.

view.name: SV-Controlled Vocabulary [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Controlled Vocabulary [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging controlled vocabulary solutions in a business-agnostic manner. This view is composed of three main elements: Business Agnostic Controlled Vocabulary Solutions, Business Agnostic Business Information Base, and Controlled Vocabulary.
The Business Agnostic Controlled Vocabulary Solutions is a Grouping ABB that encompasses several Data Object SBBs. These include eGovernment Core Vocabularies, Core Assessment Vocabulary, Core Standards and Specifications Vocabulary, W3C Profiles Vocabulary, and EuroVoc. Each of these data objects represents a specific set of vocabularies or standards used for information exchange, assessment, and description of various data entities in a context-neutral manner. For instance, the eGovernment Core Vocabularies are simplified, reusable, and extensible data models that capture the fundamental characteristics of a data entity. Similarly, the Core Assessment Vocabulary defines what an 'Assessment' of 'assets' is and how to perform the assessment based on 'Criteria'.
The Business Agnostic Business Information Base is a Diagram Model-group ABB that includes two Business Object ABBs: Data Quality and Availability. These objects represent the quality and availability of the business information, respectively.
The Controlled Vocabulary is a Data Object ABB that enables a carefully curated set of terms used to describe concepts or objects in a specific field or domain. It is a standardized list of terms that are used to ensure consistency and accuracy in the indexing, searching, and retrieval of information.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive and standardized framework for the use of controlled vocabularies in a business-agnostic manner. This ensures consistency and accuracy in the description, indexing, and retrieval of information across different business domains. It also facilitates the exchange of information and interoperability among various software solutions.

view.name: SV-Data Mapping [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Mapping [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements contained in the JSON data. The view is composed of three main elements: "Business Agnostic Business Information Base", "Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions", and "Data Mapping".
The "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" is a Diagram Model-group ABB that serves as a foundation for the business information that is not specific to any particular business. It contains two sub-elements: "Document" and "Data Quality". Both of these are Business Object ABBs, representing different types of business information. The "Document" element represents document information, while "Data Quality" represents data quality information.
The "Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions" is a Grouping ABB that serves as a catalogue for data mapping solutions that are not specific to any business. It contains one sub-element: "RDF Mapping Language (RML)". This is a Data Object SBB that describes RML, a generic mapping language based on and extending R2RML. RML is a mapping language defined to express customized mapping rules from heterogeneous data structures and serializations to the RDF data model. It is a superset of the W3C-standardized mapping language R2RML, aiming to extend its applicability and broaden its scope, adding support for data in other structured formats.
The "Data Mapping" is a Data Object ABB that aims to bring equivalence in a relationship between two data items with ontological value. It represents the process of creating data element mappings between two distinct data models.
The relationships between these elements are not explicitly defined in the JSON data, but it can be inferred that the "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" and "Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions" are related through the process of data mapping, represented by the "Data Mapping" element. The motivation behind these relationships is to provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging business-agnostic information and data mapping solutions to create equivalence between different data items.

view.name: SV-Reference Data [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Reference Data [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements and their relations to enhance the motivation and understanding of the system. The elements in the JSON are grouped into three main categories: Business Agnostic Reference Data Solutions, Business Agnostic Business Information Base, and Customs Reference Data.
The Business Agnostic Reference Data Solutions group contains a catalogue of data objects that are relevant for the EU labour market and education and training. This includes the ESCO classification, which identifies and categorises skills, competences, and occupations, and the Regulated Professions DB, which contains information on regulated professions, statistics on migrating professionals, contact points and competent authorities. This group also includes the Business Agnostic EU Vocabularies Reference Data Solutions Catalogue, which contains data objects like NUTS, Reference Data Asset, Authority Tables, and the Digital Europe Thesaurus.
The Business Agnostic Business Information Base is a diagram model-group that contains the Data Quality business object, which provides information on data quality.
The Customs Reference Data group contains a catalogue of data objects that are relevant for customs operations. This includes the Reference Data Customs Offices List, Harmonized System (HS) Codes, ISO Country Codes, Currency Code List, Unified Code for Units of Measure (UCUM), Legal and Regulatory References, and Customs Valuation Methods. This group also includes the Customs Information Base, which contains business objects like the Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI), Imports information, Exports information, Customs partners Information, Combined nomenclature, Economic value Information, Classification of goods Information, Origin of goods Information, and Economic Operators Information.
The Reference Data is a data object that enables the definition of a set of values or codes that are used to categorize, classify, or describe data elements in a consistent and standardized way.
The Diagram Model-connection ABB is an element that describes the relationships between the different elements in the system. However, the JSON does not provide any specific details about this element.

node.label: Not clear if it is an SBB in itself. It seems to be a broad description for Authority Tables and other asstets managed by the Publications Office

view.name: SV-Metadata Catalogue [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Metadata Catalogue [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the business agnostic business information base and metadata catalogue solutions.
The first element is the "Business Agnostic Business Information Base", which is a Diagram Model-group ABB. This element serves as a general framework for business information, irrespective of the specific business context. Within this base, there are two sub-elements: "Availability" and "Digital Asset". Both are Business Object ABBs, representing different types of business information. "Availability" refers to information about the availability of resources or services, while "Digital Asset" refers to information about digital resources or assets.
The second element is the "Business Agnostic Metadata Catalogue Solutions", a Grouping ABB that provides a collection of solutions for managing metadata in a business-agnostic manner. This group includes two Data Object SBBs: "Official Portal for European Data" and "JRC Data Catalogue". The "Official Portal for European Data" is a central access point for open data from various European sources, while the "JRC Data Catalogue" is a collection of metadata records about datasets produced by the Joint Research Centre (JRC), which provides scientific advice and support to the policies of the European Union.
The third element is the "Metadata Catalogue", a Data Object ABB that represents a collection of descriptive information about data, resources, or information objects related to public services. This catalogue serves as a repository for metadata, facilitating the management and utilization of data in the context of public services.
The relationships between these elements are defined by their hierarchical structure. The "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" and "Business Agnostic Metadata Catalogue Solutions" are both part of the overarching SV-Metadata Catalogue [Motivation] view, while the "Availability" and "Digital Asset" Business Object ABBs are part of the "Business Agnostic Business Information Base", and the "Official Portal for European Data" and "JRC Data Catalogue" Data Object SBBs are part of the "Business Agnostic Metadata Catalogue Solutions". The "Metadata Catalogue" stands alone as a separate element within the view.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework for managing and utilizing business information and metadata in a way that is not tied to any specific business context. This allows for greater flexibility and adaptability in the use of data and information resources.

view.name: SV-Ontology [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Ontology [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements and their relations in the JSON data. The JSON data contains several elements, each with a unique name, type, description, and elements.
The first element, "Business Agnostic Ontology Solutions," is a Grouping ABB type that contains several Data Object SBB types, including "W3C Organization," "W3C Shapes Constraint Language," "PROV-O," "FOAF," "DCAT-AP," "ADMS," "ADMS-AP," "DCAT," and "ODRL." Each of these data objects represents a different ontology solution, providing a standardized representation of various aspects of organizations, data structures, and constraints.
The second element, "Data," is a Data Object ABB type that represents symbols obtained through an encoding process of business information or a legal act.
The third element, "Business Agnostic Ontologies Catalogue Solutions," is a Grouping ABB type that contains two Data Object SBB types, "Linked Open Vocabularies (LOV)" and "ODP." These represent ontology engineering groups and semantic web portals dedicated to ontology design patterns.
The fourth element, "Ontologies Catalogue," is a Data Object ABB type that aims at indexing the collection of ontologies with comprehensiveness and trustiness value.
The fifth element, "Ontology," is a Data Object ABB type that defines a set of representational primitives with which to model a domain of knowledge or discourse.
The sixth element, "Business Agnostic Business Information Base," is a Diagram Model-group ABB type that contains three Business Object ABB types, "Availability," "Data Quality," and "Document." These represent different types of business information.
The seventh element, "Health Ontology Solutions," is a Grouping ABB type that contains several Data Object SBB types, including "International Classification of Diseases for Oncology (ICD-O)," "Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC)," "International Classification of Diseases (ICD)," "Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical Classification Ontology (ATCCO)," and "International surgery procedure ontology." Each of these data objects represents a different health ontology solution, providing a standardized representation of various aspects of health and medical data.
The eighth element, "Health Business Information Base," is a Grouping ABB type that contains three Business Object ABB types, "Diagnosis," "Laboratory," and "Operating theatre." These represent different types of health business information.
In summary, the SV-Ontology [Motivation] view provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging these elements and their relations to model a domain of knowledge or discourse, represent business and health information, and provide ontology solutions.

view.name: SV-Datasets Catalogue [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Datasets Catalogue [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements related to data cataloguing and data quality. This view is primarily composed of four main elements: 'Business Agnostic Dataset Catalogue Solutions', 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base', 'Dataset Catalogue', and 'Dataset'.
The 'Business Agnostic Dataset Catalogue Solutions' is a Grouping ABB that encompasses three Data Object SBBs: 'Eurostat Data Catalogue', 'Official Portal for European Data', and 'CELLAR'. Each of these data objects represents a unique data catalogue solution. The 'Eurostat Data Catalogue' is a comprehensive repository of statistical data maintained by EUROSTAT, the statistical office of the European Union (EU). The 'Official Portal for European Data' serves as a central point of access to European open data from various international, national, regional, local, and geodata portals. 'CELLAR' is the common data repository of the Publications Office of the European Union, storing digital publications and metadata for use by humans and machines.
The 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base' is a Diagram Model-group ABB that includes two Business Object ABBs: 'Availability' and 'Data Quality'. These objects represent critical aspects of business information, with 'Availability' referring to the accessibility of the data and 'Data Quality' referring to the integrity and reliability of the data.
The 'Dataset Catalogue' is a Data Object ABB that represents an inventory of datasets indexed in a systematic manner. This object is crucial for organizing and managing the datasets within the catalogue.
The 'Dataset' is another Data Object ABB that represents a collection of related data organized and presented in a structured format. This object is fundamental to the concept of data cataloguing as it represents the actual data that is being catalogued.
The relationships among these elements are defined by their hierarchical structure within the JSON. The 'Business Agnostic Dataset Catalogue Solutions' and 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base' are overarching elements that encompass more specific data objects and business objects, respectively. The 'Dataset Catalogue' and 'Dataset' are standalone elements that represent key aspects of the data cataloguing process. The motivation behind these elements and their relationships is to provide a comprehensive and structured approach to data cataloguing, ensuring data quality and availability.

view.name: SV-Data Syntax Mapping Catalogue [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Syntax Mapping Catalogue [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements in the given JSON. This view is designed to bridge the gap between different systems or data models, ensuring that data remains accurate and usable when transferred from a source to a destination.
The JSON contains two main elements: "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" and "Data Syntax Mapping Catalogue".
The "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" is a Diagram Model-group ABB. It is a business-agnostic model that serves as a base for business information. This base includes a sub-element named "Availability", which is a Business Object ABB. The "Availability" object represents availability information, and it does not contain any sub-elements.
The second main element in the JSON is the "Data Syntax Mapping Catalogue", which is a Data Object ABB. The description indicates that this catalogue serves as a bridge between two systems or data models. It is designed to ensure that data remains accurate and usable when it is moved from a source to a destination. This element does not contain any sub-elements.
The relationship between these two main elements is not explicitly defined in the JSON. However, based on the descriptions, it can be inferred that the "Data Syntax Mapping Catalogue" may use the "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" to ensure the accuracy and usability of data during transfer. The motivation behind this relationship is to facilitate efficient data transfer between different systems or data models, thereby enhancing the overall data management process.

view.name: SV-Data Space Policies and Contracts [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Space Policies and Contracts [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements of Data Space Policies and Contracts and Business Agnostic Business Information Base.
The Data Space Policies and Contracts is a Grouping ABB that serves as a catalogue for the elements it contains. This catalogue includes two Data Object ABBs: Data Policy and Data Contract. The Data Policy is a standalone element with no sub-elements, and it represents the policies that govern the data in the data space. The Data Contract, also a standalone element, represents the contracts that dictate the terms and conditions of data usage within the data space.
The Business Agnostic Business Information Base is a Diagram Model-group ABB that contains a collection of Business Object ABBs. These objects include Availability, Digital Asset, Credential, Access rights, and Transaction. Each of these elements represents different types of information that are business-agnostic, meaning they are not specific to any one business or industry.
The Availability object represents information about the availability of data or services. The Digital Asset object represents information about digital assets, which could include digital files, software, or other digital resources. The Credential object represents information about credentials, which could include usernames, passwords, or other forms of identification. The Access rights object represents information about access rights, which dictate who can access certain data or services. Lastly, the Transaction object represents information about transactions, which could include financial transactions, data transactions, or other types of exchanges.
