The relationships between these elements are not explicitly defined in the JSON, but it can be inferred that the Data Space Policies and Contracts catalogue governs the data represented by the Business Object ABBs in the Business Agnostic Business Information Base. This governance could include setting policies for how the data is used (Data Policy) and establishing contracts for data usage (Data Contract). The motivation behind this structure is to provide a comprehensive framework for managing data in a way that is not specific to any one business or industry, allowing for flexibility and adaptability.

view.name: SV-Data Model [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Model [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements in the JSON data. The JSON data contains three main elements: "Business Agnostic Data Model Solutions", "Business Agnostic Business Information Base", and "Data Model".
The "Business Agnostic Data Model Solutions" is a Grouping ABB type element that encompasses two sub-elements: "Common Data Model" and "eProcurement Data Model Solutions". The "Common Data Model" is a Data Object SBB type element that represents an ontology based on the FRBR model (Functional Requirements for Bibliographic Records) using RDF(S)/OWL technologies. It is capable of representing relationships between the resource types managed by the Publications Office and their views, all within the scope of the FRBR model.
The "eProcurement Data Model Solutions" is another Grouping ABB type element that includes the "ESPD-EDM" as a sub-element. The "ESPD-EDM" is a Data Object SBB type element representing the European Single Procurement Document (ESPD), a standardized form used in public procurement processes within the European Union (EU). It serves as a preliminary self-declaration by suppliers, demonstrating their eligibility and suitability to participate in public procurement procedures across EU member states.
The "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" is a Diagram Model-group ABB type element that includes three sub-elements: "Message", "Document", and "Data Quality". Each of these sub-elements is a Business Object ABB type element representing different types of business information.
Finally, the "Data Model" is a Data Object ABB type element that aims to be a collection of entities, their properties, and the relationships among them. It focuses on formally representing a domain, a concept, or a real-world thing.
The relationships among these elements are defined by their hierarchical structure in the JSON data. The motivation behind this structure is to provide a comprehensive and structured representation of different types of data models and business information, facilitating their use in various business contexts.

view.name: SV-Functional Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The view that relates Architecture principles to semantic view functional components is a relevant aspect of solutions architecture. This view focuses on how architecture principles influence the design and implementation of functional components within the semantic layer of a solution.
By aligning architecture principles with semantic view functional components, solutions architects ensure that the design and implementation of these components adhere to established guidelines and best practices. This alignment brings several benefits to the overall solution.
Firstly, it promotes consistency and coherence in the design of functional components. Architecture principles provide guidelines for designing semantic components that ensure a standardized approach and facilitate seamless integration and interoperability. By aligning functional components with these principles, solutions architects ensure that the semantics and data structures across the solution remain consistent, enabling efficient data exchange and integration.
Secondly, aligning architecture principles with semantic view functional components supports data integrity and quality. Architecture principles often emphasize data governance, data security, and data management practices. By incorporating these principles into the design and implementation of semantic components, solutions architects can enforce data governance policies, ensure data security measures, and maintain data quality standards. This alignment enhances the reliability and trustworthiness of the solution's data, leading to more accurate and informed decision-making.
Furthermore, aligning architecture principles with semantic view functional components improves the understandability and maintainability of the solution. Architecture principles provide guidelines for organizing and structuring functional components, making them easier to comprehend and manage. By aligning functional components with these principles, solutions architects facilitate future enhancements, updates, and maintenance of the solution, reducing the complexity and effort required for managing the semantic layer.

view.name: SV-Governance Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The view that relates Architecture principles to semantic view governance components is an essential aspect of solutions architecture. This view specifically focuses on how architecture principles influence the design and implementation of governance structures and processes within the semantic layer of a solution.
Aligning architecture principles with semantic view governance components brings several benefits to the overall solution.
Firstly, it ensures effective governance practices within the semantic layer. Architecture principles provide guidance on establishing governance structures, policies, and processes that govern the management and usage of data. By aligning governance components with these principles, solutions architects can design a robust governance framework that ensures compliance, transparency, and accountability in data management, access control, and data quality. This alignment promotes proper oversight and control over the semantic layer, facilitating efficient and secure data governance practices.
Secondly, aligning architecture principles with semantic view governance components supports data integrity and quality. Architecture principles often emphasize data governance, security, and management best practices. By incorporating these principles into the design and implementation of governance components, solutions architects can establish mechanisms for enforcing data governance policies, implementing security measures, and monitoring data quality. This alignment enhances the reliability and accuracy of data within the semantic layer, contributing to more informed decision-making and reliable business insights.

view.name: SV-Data Policy Catalogue
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Policy Catalogue view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the Business Agnostic Data Policy Catalogue, which is a Grouping ABB. This catalogue includes several Business Object ABBs, each with its own specific purpose and description.
The first Business Object ABB within the Business Agnostic Data Policy Catalogue is the Interoperability Policy. This policy is a set of guidelines that ensure different systems and data within an organization or across entities work together seamlessly. It promotes the use of open standards and best practices to facilitate smooth communication and integration between various systems, applications, and stakeholders.
The second Business Object ABB is the Data Quality Framework. This framework is a structured approach or set of guidelines that organizations use to assess, measure, and improve the quality of their data. It provides a systematic framework for managing data quality throughout its lifecycle, from data collection to data analysis and decision-making.
The third Business Object ABB is the Data Governance Guidelines. These guidelines are a set of principles, rules, and practices that provide direction and guidance for managing and controlling data assets within an organization. They outline the framework for ensuring data quality, integrity, privacy, security, and compliance throughout the data lifecycle.
The fourth Business Object ABB is the Blockchain policy. This policy is a set of rules, guidelines, and controls that govern the management, access, and utilization of data within a blockchain network or ecosystem. It outlines the specific protocols, procedures, and requirements for storing, validating, and securing data on the blockchain.
Lastly, the Data Policy is a standalone Business Object ABB that aims to form the guiding framework in which data management can operate. This policy is crucial in setting the direction and standards for all data-related activities within an organization.
In summary, the SV-Data Policy Catalogue view provides a comprehensive framework that includes various policies and guidelines to ensure effective data management, interoperability, quality, governance, and security. Each of these elements plays a critical role in managing and controlling data assets, promoting data integrity, privacy, and compliance, and facilitating effective data sharing and collaboration.

view.name: SV-Tax Semantic Agreements Catalogue
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Tax Semantic Agreements Catalogue view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the semantic agreements and interoperability agreements in the context of tax and tariff regulations. This view is composed of three main elements: Semantic Agreement, Semantic Interoperability Agreement, and Tax Semantic Agreements Solutions.
The Semantic Agreement, classified as a Contract ABB, formalizes an agreement from a peer to the common ontology that is the result of a matching or mapping process used to resolve their semantic discrepancies. This process involves a linguistic base, internal and external structure comparison. The result of this matching combination is used to develop an agreement unit as a component of the agreement. The agreement operates under certain assumptions, such as using the same language to represent the schema/ontology, labels, and the meaning of a concept, and there is no individual at the common ontology.
The Semantic Interoperability Agreement, also a Contract ABB, formalizes governance rules enabling collaboration between digital public services with ontological value. This agreement is crucial for ensuring seamless interaction and data exchange between different digital public services.
The Tax Semantic Agreements Solutions is a Grouping ABB that encompasses three Contract SBBs: Tax and Tariff Combined Nomenclature, WTO Nomenclature Agreements, and Tax Harmonisation Agreements. These contracts represent specific semantic agreements related to tax and tariff regulations. The Tax and Tariff Combined Nomenclature Contract outlines the combined nomenclature for tax and tariff. The WTO Nomenclature Agreements Contract details the agreements on nomenclature as per the World Trade Organization. The Tax Harmonisation Agreements Contract formalizes agreements for harmonizing tax regulations.
The relationships between these elements are primarily hierarchical, with the Semantic Agreement and Semantic Interoperability Agreement being overarching contracts that govern the specific agreements within the Tax Semantic Agreements Solutions grouping. The motivation behind this structure is to provide a comprehensive and structured approach to managing semantic agreements in the context of tax and tariff regulations, thereby facilitating semantic interoperability and collaboration between digital public services.

view.name: Digital Solution Non-Functional Requirements Catalogue viewpoint
view.documentation:
A non-functional requirements catalog for a digital solution includes a set of criteria and characteristics that describe how the solution should perform, rather than what it should do. These requirements focus on aspects such as performance, security, usability, reliability, and other quality attributes that determine the overall effectiveness and user experience of the solution.
Here are some common categories of non-functional requirements that are often included in such a catalog:
+ Performance: Defines the speed, responsiveness, scalability, and efficiency of the solution under varying conditions, such as user load, data volume, or network latency. + Usability: Specifies the ease of use, intuitiveness, and accessibility of the solution, ensuring that it meets the needs and expectations of its intended users. + Reliability: Addresses the solution's ability to consistently perform its functions accurately and reliably over time, minimizing downtime and data loss. + Security: Covers the protection of data, information, and system resources against unauthorized access, tampering, or breaches. It may include aspects such as authentication, encryption, and compliance with relevant security standards. + Availability: Describes the solution's uptime requirements, including its ability to remain accessible and operational during scheduled maintenance or unexpected outages. + Scalability: Defines the solution's ability to handle increasing workload or user demand by efficiently utilizing resources and adapting to changing circumstances. + Maintainability: Refers to the ease of maintaining and modifying the solution, including aspects such as code maintainability, documentation, and the availability of development and debugging tools. + Interoperability: Specifies the solution's ability to integrate and communicate with other systems or components, often through the use of standardized protocols or interfaces. + Compliance: Ensures that the solution adheres to relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards, such as data protection regulations or accessibility guidelines. + Performance Efficiency: Focuses on optimizing resource usage, minimizing energy consumption, and maximizing the efficiency of the solution's operations. + Testability: Defines the ease with which the solution can be tested to ensure that it meets its functional and non-functional requirements, often through the use of automated testing tools and techniques. + Internationalization and Localization: Addresses the solution's ability to support multiple languages, regions, and cultural conventions to cater to a global user base.
These are just some examples of non-functional requirements that may be included in a catalog for a digital solution. The specific requirements will depend on the nature of the solution, its intended use, and the stakeholders' needs.

view.name: Digital Solution Architecture Decisions Catalogue viewpoint
view.documentation:
The IT Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) catalogue of a digital solution refers to a collection of documents that capture and document important architectural decisions made during the development and evolution of the solution. These records serve as a valuable reference for the project team, stakeholders, and future developers, providing insights into the rationale behind key design choices and the impact of those decisions.
The ADR catalogue typically includes the following elements:
+ Title/Identifier: Each ADR is assigned a unique title or identifier to enable easy identification and retrieval. + Context: This section provides a brief overview of the background and context that led to the architectural decision. It may include factors such as business requirements, technical constraints, or market considerations. + Decision: This section outlines the specific decision made, describing the chosen solution or approach in detail. It should clearly articulate the problem being addressed and the solution chosen. + Alternatives Considered: It is essential to document alternative solutions or approaches that were evaluated before settling on the chosen decision. This helps to understand the reasoning behind the selected option. + Rationale: The rationale section explains the reasoning behind the decision. It may include factors such as performance, scalability, security, cost, maintainability, compatibility, or other relevant considerations. + Implications: This section discusses the potential impact of the decision on the system, including any anticipated benefits, drawbacks, risks, or dependencies introduced by the chosen approach. + Related ADRs: If the decision has dependencies or relationships with other ADRs, those connections should be documented in this section. It helps in establishing the traceability and understanding the interconnectedness of decisions. + Status and Date: Each ADR should include the current status (e.g., proposed, accepted, rejected, superseded) and the date when the decision was made or recorded.
By maintaining a comprehensive ADR catalogue, organizations can foster transparency, facilitate collaboration, and ensure consistency in architectural decision-making across teams and projects. It serves as a knowledge repository and assists in understanding the evolution and reasoning behind the architecture of a digital solution.

view.name: Enterprise Architecture Framework alignment guidelines viewpoint
view.documentation:
The Enterprise Architecture Framework (EAF) alignment guidelines viewpoint serves as an integral part of the process, aiming to establish a harmonious relationship between the European Interoperability Reference Architecture (EIRA) model and any given Enterprise Architecture Framework (EAF). The ultimate goal is to make the EIRA model fully compliant with the chosen EAF, promoting uniformity across the architectural ecosystem.
In this alignment diagram, each Architectural Building Block (ABB) carries a specific connection to the EIRA's Legal, Organisational, Semantic, and Technical (LOST) views that it belongs to. Each ABB forms a critical component of the architecture, representing distinct facets of the EIRA in the broader context of the selected EAF. This viewpoint connects different layers of the enterprise architecture, creating a comprehensive picture of the interoperability landscape.
The intricate ties between each ABB and their corresponding LOST views can be thoroughly explored on the [Properties] sheet under the [Analysis] tab of Archi, a visual modelling and management tool for enterprise architecture. Here, users can investigate each ABB, understanding its role, its relationship with the LOST views, and its part in securing compliance with the EAF.
The EAF alignment guidelines viewpoint allows organizations to align with industry standards, facilitates interoperability, and bridges the EIRA model with the selected EAF. It assists an organization in effectively detailing their enterprise architecture in line with their specific needs while maintaining alignment with larger industry frameworks.
The viewpoint provides a structured layout, enhancing strategic decision-making, facilitating effective communication, and aiding the integration of different architectural elements. This organized alignment fortifies the architecture's robustness and provides a pathway for strategic expansion and evolution.

view.name: TVI-Digital Workplace Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVI-Digital Workplace Infrastructure Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - infrastructure and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the capabilities of digital workplace infrastructure enablers and digital workplace enablers.
The Digital Workplace Infrastructure Enablers ABB is a Grouping that enables the set of components and services that enable organizations to create and manage virtual workplaces environments and facilitate their access remotely. This grouping includes the Remote Desktop ABB, a Technology Service that enables the procedures to grant users to access and control a computer or device from a remote location using a network connection.
The Digital Workplace Enablers is another Grouping that refers to components or services that enable the collaboration of work aspects while security and privacy are ensured. This grouping includes several Application Services and an Application Component.
The Digital Workplace ABB is both an Application Service and an Application Component that enables the procedures to freely collaborate independently from the location and boundaries while maintaining high-security standards and increasing productivity and efficiency.
The Training and Learning Management building block is an application service that helps organizations efficiently plan, administer, deliver, and track training and learning activities. It provides a comprehensive platform for managing courses, registrations, content delivery, assessments, certifications, and reporting.
The Digital Collaboration is an Application Service that facilitates digital collaboration among team members.
The Learning Platform System is a software application service that provides a comprehensive platform for managing and delivering learning content and experiences. It enables organizations to create, manage, and deliver various types of learning materials, such as courses, training modules, assessments, and educational resources.
The Remote Collaboration and Communication is a software application service that enables individuals or teams to collaborate and communicate effectively, regardless of their physical locations. It provides tools and features such as video conferencing, instant messaging, document sharing, and virtual whiteboards to support real-time or asynchronous interactions.
These elements are interconnected and work together to enable a digital workplace that is secure, efficient, and productive. The motivation behind this view is to leverage technology to facilitate remote work and collaboration, enhance learning and development, and improve organizational efficiency and productivity.

view.name: TVI-Networking Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVI-Networking Infrastructure Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - infrastructure and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various components and services that facilitate the creation and operation of computer networks. This view is divided into two main elements: Networking Infrastructure Enablers and Shared Platform.
The Networking Infrastructure Enablers ABB is a grouping of components and services that include both hardware and software technologies essential for building and maintaining modern networks. It consists of several elements such as Private Network, Firewall, Load Balancer, Router, Private Subnetwork, Domain Name Service, Virtual Private Network, and Gateway. These elements enable the implementation of various network functionalities such as physical communication, network security, traffic distribution, network connection, IP address translation, and protocol conversion.
The Shared Platform ABB is an application component that sets technical reusable resources with convergence power, enabling interoperability from a technical perspective across levels in a public administration, cross public administrations, and cross borders. It includes several groupings such as API Enablers, Orchestration Enablers, Security Enablers, Test Enablers, Trust Enablers, Data Exchange Enablers, Data Management Enablers, Privacy Enablers, Knowledge Discovery Enablers, Analytics Enablers, Translation Enablers, Digital Workplace Enablers, Artificial Intelligence Enablers, Dataspace Enablers, Schedule Management Enablers, Messaging Enablers, Observability and Monitoring Enablers, and Containerization Enablers. These groupings refer to components and services that support various functionalities such as software interfaces, orchestration applications, security controls, conformance testing, secure-cross borders transactions, data exchange, data management, privacy-related functionality, knowledge discovery, data analysis, language translation, digital workplace, artificial intelligence, dataspace creation, schedule management, messaging, observability and monitoring, and containerization.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework that leverages various components and services to facilitate the creation and operation of computer networks. This framework aims to enable interoperability from a technical perspective across levels in a public administration, cross public administrations, and cross borders. It also supports various functionalities such as software interfaces, orchestration applications, security controls, conformance testing, secure-cross borders transactions, data exchange, data management, privacy-related functionality, knowledge discovery, data analysis, language translation, digital workplace, artificial intelligence, dataspace creation, schedule management, messaging, observability and monitoring, and containerization.

view.name: TVI-Data Management and Knowledge Discovery Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVI-Data Management and Knowledge Discovery Infrastructure Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - infrastructure and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements related to data management and knowledge discovery.
The view consists of several Grouping ABBs, each containing multiple elements. The first Grouping ABB is "Database Infrastructure Enablers", which enables tools and technology services for efficient data management and operation under a storage system. It includes Technology Service ABBs such as "Relational Database Manager", "Object-Oriented Database Manager", "NoSQL Database Manager", "Graph Database Manager", and "Database Cache Manager". These services implement the behavior of various software systems that manage and manipulate different types of databases.
The second Grouping ABB is "Storage Infrastructure Enablers", which facilitates efficient and effective data storage. It includes Technology Service ABBs like "File Storage", "Block Storage", "Distributed File System", and "Backup". These services implement the behavior of software tools that manage data storage in various forms.
The third Grouping ABB is "Data Lake Infrastructure Enablers", which helps organizations build and maintain a robust data lake infrastructure. It includes a Technology Service ABB called "Data Lake Storage", which implements the behavior of a storage repository that allows organizations to store large amounts of structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data at any scale.
The fourth Grouping ABB is "Data Management Enablers", which supports effective data management practices and procedures. It includes Application Component ABBs and Application Service ABBs such as "Data Publication", "Forms Management", "Content Management", "Data Management", "e-Archiving", "Metadata Management", "Data Quality", "Data Extraction, Transformation, and Loading", "Data Persistence", "Data Virtualization", "Multimedia distribution", "Submission Service", "Transaction Management", "Archival Information Packages", "Trusted Digital Repositories", "Service Metadata Publisher", "CRM", "Data Publication", "Forms Management", "Data Extraction, Transformation and Loading", "Data Virtualization", "eFiles Management", "Service Metadata Locator", "Open Data Management", and "Contact Management". These services and components enable various functionalities related to data management.
The fifth Grouping ABB is "Knowledge Discovery Enablers", which facilitates the process of discovering insights and knowledge from data. It includes an Application Component ABB called "Knowledge Discovery" and a Data Object ABB called "Knowledge Triplestore", which enable the extraction of previously unknown, potentially useful information from data.
The final Grouping ABB is "Dataspace Enablers", which supports the creation and management of a dataspace. It includes Application Service ABBs such as "Dataspace", "Dataspace Connector", "Dataspace Connector Consumer", and "Dataspace Connector Provider". These services enable the creation of a single market for data by integrating, transforming, and making available such data.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements related to data management and knowledge discovery, enabling organizations to effectively manage their data and extract valuable insights from it.

view.name: TVI-Management Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVI-Management Infrastructure Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - infrastructure and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that enable the management of IT platforms, data spaces, security, privacy, and orchestration in a public administration context.
The view is divided into several groupings, each containing elements that contribute to the overall management infrastructure. The first grouping, API Enablers, includes components and frameworks that support the implementation and cataloguing of open software interfaces. This includes elements like the Service Registry, which enables the registering of system services, and the API Catalogue, which is a collection of open software interfaces.
The second grouping, Management Infrastructure Enablers, refers to the set of components and services that manage a public administration's IT platforms efficiently. This includes elements like the Logger, which records events within a system, and the Management Console, which provides a centralised interface for managing and monitoring digital platforms.
The third grouping, Dataspace Enablers, refers to components and services that support the creation and management of a dataspace. This includes elements like the Dataspace, which is a virtual space for integrating and making data available, and the Dataspace Connector, which enables easy and trustworthy data sharing.
The fourth grouping, Security Enablers, includes components that enable the implementation and management of security controls and measures. This includes elements like the Audit, which ensures the correct behaviour, security, and compliance of different building blocks.
The fifth grouping, Privacy Enablers, refers to components and services that facilitate the implementation of privacy-related functionality. This includes elements like the Privacy service, which enables functionalities such as storing, securing, and anonymising personal data.
The final grouping, Orchestration Enablers, refers to the components and practices that support the development and deployment of orchestration applications. This includes elements like the Orchestration service, which defines the sequence and conditions in which one service invokes other services.
Overall, the TVI-Management Infrastructure Enablers [Motivation] view provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements to enable efficient and effective management of IT platforms, data spaces, security, privacy, and orchestration in a public administration context.

view.name: TVI-Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVI-Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - infrastructure and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) in an organization. This view is composed of two main groupings: Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Enablers and Artificial Intelligence Enablers.
The Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Enablers grouping refers to a set of components that facilitate the development and deployment of artificial intelligence applications. Within this grouping, there is a Technology Service ABB named Machine Learning. This service enables the procedures for implementing algorithms and models that can learn from and make predictions on data. The Machine Learning service is a critical component of the AI infrastructure, providing the necessary tools and capabilities for data analysis and predictive modeling.
The Artificial Intelligence Enablers grouping refers to components and services that provide the necessary infrastructure and resources for AI developers to build intelligent systems. These systems can perform tasks that typically require human-like intelligence, such as perception, reasoning, learning, and decision-making. Within this grouping, there are several elements:
1. Artificial Intelligence as an Application Service ABB: This service enables the procedures to display intelligent behavior by analyzing their environment and taking actions with some degree of autonomy to achieve specific objectives.
2. Artificial Intelligence as an Application Component ABB: This component enables the implementation of algorithms, machine learning, and deep learning techniques to enable machines to perform tasks that typically require human-like intelligence.
3. Machine Learning as an Application Service ABB: This service enables systems to automatically learn and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed. It involves the development and deployment of algorithms and models that can analyze large volumes of data, identify patterns, and make predictions or decisions based on the learned patterns.
4. Artificial Intelligence Engine as an Application Service ABB: This service refers to a software component or service that encompasses the core capabilities of an AI system. It provides a set of algorithms, models, and tools that enable the development, deployment, and execution of AI applications.
5. Natural-Language Processing (NLP) as an Application Service ABB: This service enables the understanding, interpretation, and generation of human language in a valuable way.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging AI capabilities, facilitating the development and deployment of AI applications, and providing the necessary infrastructure for AI developers to build intelligent systems.

view.name: TVI-Wide Area Networking [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVI-Wide Area Networking [Motivation] view extends Technical view - infrastructure and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging different types of networks to enable communication and data exchange across geographically dispersed locations. This view is primarily composed of two main elements: 'Wide Area Networking' and 'Secure Public Network Solutions'.
The 'Wide Area Networking' is a Grouping ABB that encompasses different networks to facilitate communication and data exchange. Within this grouping, there are two Communication Network ABBs: 'Public Network' and 'Secure Public Network'. The 'Public Network' is a communication network that allows access to the public, including public administrations, businesses, and citizens, without specific authorisations. Interoperable European Solutions can rely on these Public Networks, such as the Internet, to realise the physical communication between nodes. On the other hand, the 'Secure Public Network' is a communication network that also enables public access but is specifically designed and configured to protect against unauthorized access and cyber threats.
The second main element in this view is the 'Secure Public Network Solutions', another Grouping ABB. This grouping includes two Communication Network SBBs: 'Common Communication Network (CCN)' and 'Common Communication Network 2 (CCN 2)'. Both of these networks are part of the Secure Public Network Solutions, indicating that they are designed to provide secure communication channels.
In terms of relations and motivations, the 'Wide Area Networking' grouping is motivated by the need to enable communication and data exchange across geographically dispersed locations. The inclusion of both 'Public Network' and 'Secure Public Network' within this grouping suggests a motivation to cater to different levels of security requirements. Similarly, the 'Secure Public Network Solutions' grouping, including the 'CCN' and 'CCN 2' networks, is motivated by the need for secure communication solutions. The presence of these two networks indicates a motivation to provide options for secure communication, catering to different needs or contexts.

view.name: TVI-Trust Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVI-Trust Infrastructure Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - infrastructure and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various components and services to build a secure and trustworthy environment for data sharing and transactions.
The view consists of several elements grouped into four main categories: Blockchain Infrastructure Enablers, Trust Infrastructure Enablers, Trust Enablers, and Dataspace Enablers.
Blockchain Infrastructure Enablers ABB is a grouping of components and services that allow for the construction of a digital ledger infrastructure of interconnected nodes. This includes the Immutable Database Manager ABB, Blockchain Ledger ABB, and Distributed Blockchain Network ABB. These technology services enable the management of immutable data, recording and sharing of transactions in an electronic ledger, and the implementation of tokens in a blockchain network, respectively.
Trust Infrastructure Enablers ABB is a grouping devoted to creating and managing public keys for encryption, a common method of securing data transfers on the internet. This includes the PKI Certificate Manager ABB, a technology service that enables the issuance, maintenance, and revocation of public key certificates.
Trust Enablers ABB is a grouping that facilitates the establishment and maintenance of secure cross-border transactions and interactions. It includes several application services such as e-Seal Preservation, e-Timestamp Verification and Validation, Registered Electronic Delivery, e-Seal Verification and Validation, e-Signature Creation, e-Signature Preservation, e-Signature Verification and Validation, e-Seal Creation, and e-Timestamp Creation. These services enable various procedures related to electronic signatures, timestamps, and seals, extending their trustworthiness and verifying their validity.
Dataspace Enablers ABB is a grouping that supports the creation and management of a dataspace. It includes the Dataspace, Dataspace Connector, Dataspace Connector Consumer, and Dataspace Connector Provider application services. These services enable the creation of a single market for data, easy and trustworthy data sharing, data gathering and accessibility, and control over data use in the dataspace ecosystem, respectively.
The motivation behind these groupings and services is to provide a secure and trustworthy environment for data sharing and transactions, leveraging blockchain technology, trust infrastructure, and dataspace capabilities. This view provides a comprehensive framework for understanding and implementing these elements in a cohesive and effective manner.

view.name: TVI-Analytics Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVI-Analytics Infrastructure Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - infrastructure and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements of the Analytics Infrastructure Enablers and Analytics Enablers.
The Analytics Infrastructure Enablers is a Grouping ABB that refers to the set of components and services that support the development and deployment of data analytics solutions. This group includes four Technology Service ABBs: Analytics, Business Intelligence, Databricks, and Data Catalog.
The Analytics ABB is a Technology service that enables the procedures of analysing a great amount of raw data to make conclusions about specific information. The Business Intelligence ABB is a Technology Service that enables the procedure of collecting, storing, and analysing the data produced by the public administration to improve and optimise decisions and performance. The Databricks ABB is a Technology Service that enables the procedures of a collaborative workspace to process large amounts of public administration data. The Data Catalog ABB is a Technology Service that enables the procedures of a centralised metadata repository to provide information about the data assets in a public administration.
The Analytics Enablers is another Grouping ABB that refers to components and services that serve any current or future Digital Service Infrastructure (DSI) requiring data analysis capabilities. This group includes five Application Component and Service ABBs: Data Analytics, Big Data Analytics, Data Analytics, Business Intelligence, and Smart queue management.
The Data Analytics ABB is an Application Component that enables the implementation of procedures to analyze data and extract insights that can be used to improve business decision-making, optimize business processes, and drive innovation. The Big Data Analytics Application service refers to a software application or platform that leverages advanced analytics techniques to process and analyze large and complex datasets, commonly known as big data. It enables organizations to derive valuable insights, identify patterns, trends, and correlations, and make data-driven decisions. The service typically includes data ingestion, storage, processing, and visualization capabilities, as well as advanced analytics techniques such as machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive modeling. The Data Analytics ABB is an Application Service that enables the use of procedures to analyze data and extract insights that can be used to improve business decision-making, optimize business processes, and drive innovation. The Business Intelligence and Smart Queue Management are both Application Services with unspecified descriptions in this context.
The motivation behind these elements and their relations is to provide a comprehensive framework that supports the development, deployment, and enhancement of data analytics solutions, enabling better decision-making, business process optimization, and innovation within the public administration.

view.name: TVI-Containers Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
Narrative: The Orchestration Infrastructure Enablers view provides insights into the relationship between the infrastructure enablers for orchestration and the orchestration enablers at the application level. This view highlights the importance of a robust and efficient infrastructure to support the seamless coordination and automation of business processes.
At the infrastructure layer, several elements are involved in enabling orchestration. The Management Infrastructure Enablers play a vital role in providing the necessary tools and capabilities for managing and monitoring the orchestration processes. These enablers include components such as logger technology services, audit manager technology services, telemetry technology services, and management console technology services. They enable organizations to effectively manage and control the execution of orchestrated workflows.
Additionally, the Workflow Orchestration Infrastructure Enablers provide the foundational components for modelling, executing, and monitoring complex business workflows. These enablers encompass workflow engines, service buses, event managers, and process managers. They are designed to support the seamless execution and coordination of business processes across different systems and services.
Furthermore, the Containers Infrastructure Enablers play a crucial role in providing the necessary runtime environment for orchestrating and deploying containerized applications. These enablers include container orchestrator technology services, container manager technology services, container registry technology services, and containers themselves. They enable organizations to encapsulate and manage their applications in lightweight, isolated containers, facilitating easy deployment and scalability.
The orchestration enablers at the application level work in collaboration with the infrastructure enablers to facilitate the seamless automation of business processes. These enablers include components and services that support activities such as process modelling, integration, event handling, and service orchestration. They empower organizations to define and automate their business workflows, integrating disparate systems and services into cohesive end-to-end processes.
The synergy between the orchestration infrastructure enablers and the orchestration enablers at the application level is essential for the success of process automation initiatives. The infrastructure enablers provide the necessary runtime environment, management capabilities, and containerization support to execute orchestrated processes, while the orchestration enablers empower organizations to design and configure complex business workflows.
By establishing a strong connection between the orchestration infrastructure enablers and the orchestration enablers at the application level, organizations can achieve streamlined and efficient business operations. This enables organizations to automate repetitive tasks, improve process visibility and control, and enhance overall operational efficiency.

view.name: TVI-Computing Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVI-Computing Infrastructure Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - infrastructure and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various components and services that facilitate the development, deployment, and management of virtual and computing infrastructure. This view is divided into several groups, each containing different elements that contribute to the overall computing infrastructure.
The first group, "Computing Infrastructure Enablers", includes two Node ABBs: "Virtual Machine" and "Server". The Virtual Machine ABB enables the emulation of a physical computer to run programs and deploy applications, while the Server ABB enables access to resources or services to other computers or devices on a network.
The second group, "Artificial Intelligence Enablers", contains several Application Service ABBs and Application Component ABBs that provide the necessary infrastructure and resources for AI developers to build intelligent systems. These include "Artificial Intelligence", "Machine learning", "Artificial Intelligence Engine", and "Natural-Language Processing (NLP)".
The third group, "Analytics Enablers", refers to components and services that serve any current or future Digital Service Infrastructure (DSI) requiring data analysis capabilities. This group includes "Data Analytics", "Big Data Analytics", "Business Intelligence", and "Smart queue management".
The fourth group, "Data Management Enablers", refers to components and services that support effective data management practices and procedures. This group includes "Data Publication", "Forms Management", "Content Management", "Data Management", "e-Archiving", "Metadata Management", "Data Quality", "Data Extraction, Transformation, and Loading", "Data Persistence", "Data Virtualization", "Multimedia distribution", "Submission Service", "Transaction Management", "Archival Information Packages", "Trusted Digital Repositories", "Service Metadata Publisher", "CRM", "Data Publication", "Forms Management", "Data Extraction, Transformation and Loading", "Data Virtualization", "eFiles Management", "Service Metadata Locator", "Open Data Management", "Contact Management".
The fifth group, "Orchestration Enablers", refers to the components and practices that support the development and deployment of orchestration applications. This group includes "Orchestration" and "Workflow Management".
The final group, "Data Exchange Enablers", refers to tools or components that facilitate the exchange of data between systems or applications. This group includes "Data Exchange", "Once-Only Technical System", and "Data Exchange".
Each of these groups and their elements play a crucial role in the overall computing infrastructure, providing the necessary tools and services to facilitate the development, deployment, and management of various applications and systems.

view.name: TVI-Application Integration Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVI-Application Integration Infrastructure Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - infrastructure and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that facilitate the integration of disparate applications and systems within an organization.
The view is divided into several groupings, each containing elements that serve specific functions. The first grouping is the "Application Integration Infrastructure Enablers", which includes technology services such as the Enterprise Service Bus, API Manager, GraphQL Server, Serverless Orchestrator, Application Server, Event Manager, and API Gateway. These services enable the integration between applications by performing various tasks such as data transformation, connectivity handling, message routing, communication protocol conversion, and managing the composition of multiple requests.
The second grouping is "API Enablers", which refers to components and frameworks that support the implementation and cataloguing of software interfaces. This includes application components like the Service Registry and API Catalogue, and application interfaces such as Web Service, API, ePayment, eInvoicing, eTendering, eProfessional Qualification, Geo-Localization, eProcurement, Supply Chain Management, eQualification, eNotification, ERP System, Financial Management, Log Management, Service Discovery and Registry, API Discovery and Catalogue, and Service Registry.
The third grouping is "Content Delivery Infrastructure Enablers", which includes technology services like the Web Server and Streaming Server. These services enable the delivery of digital content such as web pages, videos, images, and audio files to end-users.
The fourth grouping is "Management Infrastructure Enablers", which includes technology services like Logger, Audit Manager, Telemetry, and Management Console. These services enable the efficient management of a public administration's IT platforms.
The final grouping is "Dataspace Enablers", which includes application services like Dataspace, Dataspace Connector, Dataspace Connector Consumer, and Dataspace Connector Provider. These services support the creation and management of a dataspace, enabling the integration, transformation, and availability of data.
Each of these elements plays a crucial role in the overall application integration infrastructure, contributing to the efficient and effective functioning of an organization's IT systems. The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework that facilitates the integration of disparate applications and systems, thereby enhancing the organization's operational efficiency and effectiveness.

view.name: TVI-Access and Identity Infrastructure Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
Narrative: The Identity Access Infrastructure focuses on managing user identities and their access privileges. It encompasses the [Identity Provider Technology Service], which enables the secure identification and authentication of users, and the [Federated Identity Provider Technology Service], which allows seamless integration with external identity providers. Additionally, the [Lightweight Directory Access Technology Service] facilitates efficient storage and retrieval of user and access information.
To strengthen security and privacy within the technical view, the access and identity infrastructure relates to various security application services. These services include robust encryption mechanisms, secure communication protocols, and threat detection and prevention systems. By integrating these security application services, the access and identity infrastructure ensures the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of sensitive data and resources.
Moreover, privacy enablers are incorporated into the access and identity infrastructure to comply with privacy regulations and protect user data. These enablers encompass mechanisms for data anonymization, consent management, and data retention policies. By implementing these privacy enablers, organizations can demonstrate their commitment to privacy protection and establish trust with their users.
By extending the narrative to include the Technical view - access and identity infrastructure, organizations can establish a secure and privacy-conscious foundation for their digital solutions. This view leverages the Management Infrastructure Enablers and Identity Access Infrastructure, while integrating security application services and privacy enablers to safeguard sensitive information, ensure proper user authentication and authorization, and adhere to privacy regulations. By doing so, organizations can provide a trusted and secure environment for their users while maintaining compliance with relevant security and privacy standards.

view.name: TVI-Governance Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The view connects Architecture principles to technical view and the governance components. It is a relevant aspect of solutions architecture. This view specifically examines how architecture principles influence the design and implementation of governance structures within the application layer of a solution.
Firstly, it establishes effective governance within the application layer. Architecture principles provide guidance on defining governance structures, policies, and processes for application and infrastructure development and management. By aligning governance components with these principles, solutions architects design a robust governance framework that promotes compliance, transparency, and accountability in application development, configuration, and operations. This alignment ensures proper control and management of applications, reducing risks and enhancing overall governance practices.
Secondly, aligning architecture principles with governance components supports optimized application development and deployment. Architecture principles often emphasize best practices for application design, scalability, and performance optimization. By incorporating these principles into the design and implementation of governance components, solutions architects establish mechanisms for enforcing design patterns, scalability approaches, and performance monitoring.

view.name: TVI-Functional Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The view that relates Architecture principles to infrastructure layer view functional components is crucial in solutions architecture. This view focuses on how architecture principles influence the design and implementation of functional components within the technical layer.
By aligning architecture principles with technical layer view functional components, solutions architects ensure consistency, enhance performance and scalability, promote reusability and maintainability, and support regulatory compliance. This alignment leads to the creation of robust and efficient applications within the technology layer, enabling seamless integration, optimal user experience, reduced maintenance effort, and adherence to legal and industry standards.
In summary, aligning Architecture principles with technical layer view functional components ensures consistency, enhances performance and scalability, promotes reusability and maintainability, and supports regulatory compliance. By following these principles, solutions architects can design robust and efficient applications within the technical layer.
